Honor? I learned long ago there is no such thing. Honor is but a myth. Death, vengeance and despair - these are real.
Tell me, <FirstName> - how can you go on, knowing you fight for a city that is doomed to fall when the Old Ones return?
Let me live? You can do no such thing, <FirstName>. You serve Neverwinter, you have no choice but to end my existence.
Death might actually be a blessing for me, in any case. I grow so very weary with this life.
I have seen the future in my dreams, <FirstName>. Neverwinter will vanish in a blaze of flame when the Old Ones are reborn - it is inevitable.
I am at your mercy, <FirstName>. Ask your questions and I will answer them.
Is the execution of my lover not justification enough for what I have become? They say I betrayed Neverwinter, but Neverwinter betrayed Fenthick first!
Hope? All hope within my heart perished with Fenthick. He was taken from me, the light of my life, and I was left alone in the empty darkness.
With Fenthick's death I lost more than a lover! He was a devoted servant of both Tyr and Neverwinter, and I saw how his devotion was repaid!

How could I believe in a god who allowed such an atrocity? How could I serve a city so mercilessly cruel? When Fenthick was executed I lost my lover, my faith, my loyalty - everything I believed in crumbled around me!
I know this, <FirstName>. And yet, I would speak with you before you end my life. So you might understand why I did what I did.
Maugrim has the Word of Power in his room - through the door to the east. We knew you were coming, <FirstName>. That is why I am here rather than leading Luskan's army.
I was supposed to defend Maugrim from you. But in this, like in everything else, I have failed.
What can I tell you of the Queen of the Old Ones that you do not already know? She is ancient and cruel, powerful and cunning.
Even now her spectre has descended upon the city, inflaming the spirits of the Luskan army and drowning Neverwinter's defenders in hopeless despair.
The world we know will be consumed in the flames of Morag's return, until only the bitter ashes of sorrow and death remain.
I... I am simply telling you what happened, <FirstName>. How I... how I came to break my vows and betray all that I stood for.
Fenthick's death set in motion events that could not be stopped. In the end Morag will awaken the Old Ones and we are all doomed.
I have chosen a path of hatred and bloody vengeance, and from this path there is no escape. It is too late for me. It is too late for us all.
Perhaps... perhaps you are right. Perhaps, had I acted differently... but it is too late for me now, <FirstName>.
Look around you, <FirstName>. Look at the death and destruction I have brought to Neverwinter. I can never make up for this.
And I have been too long under Morag's power. The Queen has a... a hold on me. I could not stand with you against her, even if... even if I wanted to. I cannot help the city.
I could bring my information to Lord Nasher and Aarin Gend, true. But it would not be enough to turn the tide of the battle. Morag's power will bring victory to the Luskan troops.
Perhaps a few hundred lives could be saved, though the city would still fall. But what will that avail me? Lord Nasher would still have me executed for what I have done.
<StartCheck>[Failure]</Start> Do you think I am a fool, <FirstName>? I know Lord Nasher too well to believe such tripe!
I should sacrifice myself for the sake of the people who demanded Fenthick's blood? Do you really believe me capable of so selfless an act, <FirstName>?
Once I would have gladly sacrificed myself for this city. But I have changed, <FirstName>. I am no longer the Aribeth you knew. Now I walk a different path.
<StartCheck>[Success]</Start> Your words are... wise, <FirstName>. Perhaps... perhaps I can set aside my hatred.
<StartCheck>[Success]</Start> There... there is a part of me that still weeps when I see the destruction of Neverwinter. Perhaps... perhaps you are right, <FirstName>.
If I... if I turn myself over to Lord Nasher for execution... Many lives may yet be saved. At least... at least then my own death would have some meaning.
<StartCheck>[Failure]</Start> You are wasting your time, <FirstName>. I am beyond your power to save.
You... you kept my ring? After my betrayal? After all the death and misery I have brought to you and the city? But... but why?
I... I am not who I once was, <FirstName>. I... I cannot... it would not be possible... I cannot go back. Not after what I have done.
Your words are... wise, <FirstName>. Perhaps... perhaps I can set aside my hatred.
There... there is a part of me that still weeps when I see the destruction of Neverwinter. Perhaps... perhaps you are right, <FirstName>.
But you... you will have to trust me in this, <FirstName>. Maugrim waits for you behind this door, you must face him now - time is of the essence.
Then... I shall leave Maugrim to you, and I... I shall deliver myself to Lord Nasher and tell him what I know of the Luskan troop movements.
If we are lucky, my information may help some of Neverwinter's citizens escape with their lives. And I... I will submit to Lord Nasher's judgment, whatever the consequences may be.
I am grateful to you for this, <FirstName>- this chance to... to do what is right. I wanted you to know that before I go, in case... in case Lord Nasher has me executed before you return.
Lady Aribeth? It has been a long time since anyone called me that. Thank you, <FirstName>.
Your words are kind, <FirstName>, but I am ready for whatever awaits.
No, <FirstName>. If I run away it will mean I have learned nothing. I am ready to accept the consequences of what I have done - whatever those consequences may be.
No! I... I dare not. I have served Morag for too long. She had a... a hold over me. I am afraid if I must face her or Maugrim I might once again fall under her sway.
I... I must go to Lord Nasher now, while my resolve is still strong. You must face Maugrim without me. Goodbye, <FirstName> - and good luck.
It is good to see you again, <FirstName>. When I surrendered to Lord Nasher I was certain my execution would be swift.
I understand. There is still much that must be done if Morag is to be defeated. I wish you luck, <FirstName>.
I have already given most of my information to Aarin Gend and Lord Nasher - Luskan battle plans and the location of their troops. But I will try to help you however I can.
The Old Ones are an ancient and evil race distantly related to the lizardmen of our own time. Morag was their queen during the height of their empire.
But the world changed and the North became a frozen waste, and Morag placed her people in a magical stasis within the Source Stone to await the time of their awakening.
More than this I cannot say. When I served Morag I cared little for the reasons behind the attack on Neverwinter. I only cared about revenge. But I am finally free of that burden.
The Source Stone is a great gem located in long forgotten chambers beneath Castle Never. Within this gem is an entire other world, a realm where Morag and her people await the time of the awakening.
I know the Words of Power were somehow connected with raising Morag and her people from their slumber, but beyond this there is little I can tell you.
As you know, there were four Words of Power. At first, Maugrim seemed to believe we would need to possess all four Words to awaken Morag.
However, as Morag's power grew she sent Maugrim a vision of a ritual that could begin the awakening with only one of the Words.
But the ritual was only partially successful. Morag was awakened - but she was still trapped within the Source Stone.
In time Morag's power will grow until she is able to release herself and her people from the Source Stone, but for now she is trapped inside. I wish I could tell you more, but that is all I know.
I... I suppose I should not be surprised by your anger. I make no effort to defend my actions, though I thought you, of all people, might not judge me so harshly.
I hope... I hope you will one day set aside your hate, as I have set aside mine. Perhaps then we can speak as we once did.
I am a prisoner and a fallen paladin. The powers Tyr once granted me are gone, as are the abilities Morag bestowed upon me.
And yet, for the first time since Fenthick's death, I am whole once more. I feel grief over what has happened, of course, and deep regret over what I have done. But I also feel a great calm.
I have you to thank for this, <FirstName>. Without your intervention I would never have found this peace.
I am ready to meet my fate, <FirstName>. There is a great peace upon me now.
There are worse things than death. I know this now. And Nasher has not passed judgment upon me yet.
I am content with whatever fate awaits me, yet in his eyes I see reason to hope I might yet live. If Neverwinter should survive, perhaps Lord Nasher has other plans for me.
I may yet be given the chance to make amends for all I have done, <FirstName> - though I know I will never be able to fully atone for what I have done.
But it seems Lord Nasher has chosen to let me live... for now, at least. I am glad, if for no other reason than it gives me a chance to see you again.
I am at peace, <FirstName> - for the first time since Fenthick's death. And I have you to thank. You saved me.
I no longer fear my fate, <FirstName>. When Fenthick... when Fenthick was executed I thought I had lost everything. But now I see this is not true.
I have you, <FirstName>. You were there when I was in my darkest hour, you were there when I needed you - but I was too blind to see.
But you never gave up on me. I have found myself again, <FirstName>. And I finally see how... how special you are to me.
I understand, <FirstName> - you have every right to feel that way. I only wanted to tell you the truth that is within my own heart.
You have done more for me than you can ever know, and for this I will always have special feelings for you.
But I see this makes you uncomfortable, so we shall speak of this no more. Is there something else I might do for you?
They say it is better to have loved and lost than not to have loved at all. I never used to believe that, <FirstName>.. until now.
I loved Fenthick with all my heart, and his memory will always be dear to me. But that does not mean I can never love another. Perhaps in time we might... if things had been different...
Lord Nasher has not passed judgment on me yet. I am content with whatever fate awaits, but in his eyes I see hope that I might live.
Should Neverwinter survive, he may chose another sentence for me. I may yet be given a chance to make some small amends for what I have done. There is yet hope for me... and for us.
Forgive me for speaking so frankly about this, <FirstName>. My heart could not stay silent, but I should not have burdened you with this - not while you still must face Morag.
If fate is kind, perhaps we will be able to continue this once Morag is slain. But while she lives we must set our own feelings aside for the greater good.
Perhaps if I had learned this lesson long ago, tragedy could have been averted. Forgive me, but I will speak of my feelings for you no more. You must concentrate on the task at hand.
Please, <FirstName> - we have both made our feelings toward each other clear. But Morag still lives; now is not the time for this discussion.
This I cannot do, <FirstName>. Even if Lord Nasher chose to release me from this cell, I would have to refuse your request.
I served too long under the Queen of the Old Ones. She has a... a hold over me. A power I fear I might not be able to resist.
I will not put myself in the position where I might betray Neverwinter again. I have learned from my mistakes.
But I dare not accompany you, for fear I will fall once again under Morag's spell. Do you trust me enough to let me go, if I vow to surrender myself to Lord Nasher? Can you take that risk?
My fate is in Lord Nasher's hands now.
I see Morag was right, <FullName> - Aribeth was not strong enough to defeat you. But she has served her purpose.
You have come too late, the ritual is over, the awakening of the Old Ones has begun!
The Creator Race will be reborn - and you shall be the first to taste the power my Queen has given unto me!
Fools! I cannot be so easy slain!
I am reborn! The Queen of the Old Ones has made me immortal!
No - no, this cannot be! I am immortal! No!! NOOOO!!!
The golems, there's... *ungh* there's no defeating them...
His massive blade, it cut me right - *agh!* - right there...
I'd like to get my hands on whoever's controlling it, I tell ya...
I need to see the Source Stone.
I would like to ask you some questions.
Me need see stone.
Me want ask questions.
Goodbye.

What you know 'bout Source Stone?
Where are the Words of Power?
Where be Power Words?
Who are you again?
Who you be again?
Don't you think it might be dangerous to unlock the secrets of the Source Stone?
You not think it dangerous to unlock secrets of stone?
How come nobody noticed this stone down here before?
This stone be here long time. How come no one see it 'til now?
<StartCheck>[Insight]</Start> You feel the call of the ancient evil that dwells within the stone, Master Ford. Beware lest it consume you.
Tell me your theories.
Me want hear your theories.
I'm not interested in your theories.
Me not interested in you theory.
Greetings, I am Master Ford, head archeologist of Neverwinter. Lord Nasher mentioned someone might be coming to investigate the Source Stone. <FullName>, isn't it?
Feel free to speak to me again anytime, <FullName>. I'm always eager to discuss the Source Stone.
I tried to pry some of its secrets from Haedraline - the lizard creature Lord Nasher has imprisoned in the dungeons. But she didn't seem to trust me.
Uh... yes. Yes, of course. Why should I be the only one allowed to see it? It isn't mine, after all. Go right in and take a look if you want.
Of course, I'm happy to share my knowledge with you. I feel my theories on the secrets of the Source Stone are somewhat wasted on my students.
Goodness - you are a thick one, aren't you?
The stone radiates a magical heat strong enough to keep the entire city warm even in this chill climate, yet gentle enough that you can actually go right up and touch the stone itself.
That is all we really know for certain. However, I have several theories based on my own examinations and extensive research into ancient manuscripts.
They're with the Source Stone. I thought they might be the key to unlocking it's secrets, but they didn't work. Perhaps something is missing.
Back again, <FullName>? Is there something I can do for you?
The Source Stone is truly a remarkable discovery, I must say. Fascinating. I've been an archeologist for nearly half a century and I've never come across anything like it before.
I doubt it will do you much good, however. There doesn't seem to be any way to unlock the secrets of the stone. I thought the Words of Power might be the key, but they haven't done anything so far.
Esmerelda thinks we shouldn't be tampering with the Source Stone. And Cletus is as ignorant as he is arrogant. I gave him some old texts to read to keep him out of my hair.
I am Master Ford, Neverwinter's foremost expert in ancient artifacts and historical treasures. In short, an archeologist.
When the Source Stone was discovered here beneath Castle Never, Lord Nasher wisely appointed me to investigate its secrets. What I have uncovered so far has been fascinating!
You sound like my assistant Esmerelda. She wants nothing to do with the stone. But I am well aware of the risks involved.
And yet... I cannot leave the stone alone. When awake it consumes my thoughts and at night it haunts my dreams. It calls to me... it *wants* me to unravel the mysteries contained within!
It was only after that lizard creature Haedraline told us of the Source Stone's existence that we began to search beneath the dungeons of Castle Never for hidden passages.
We found the secret door easily enough, then. It was almost too easy, considering nobody ever noticed it before. It's almost like the Source Stone itself *wants* to be found now.
My assistant Esmerelda said the same thing. I'll tell you what I told her - I'm an experienced archeologist. I know what I'm doing. Don't worry about me.
The Source Stone is surrounded by four pedestals. I placed a Word of Power on each pedestal, but of course there were only three Words.
I suspect there is a fourth Word that is necessary to unlock the Source Stone. Four pedestals, four Words of Power. Just a theory, of course, but a fairly logical conclusion.
Ah, well. Perhaps some other time, then. Is there something else you need?

My research indicates that there is an entire extra-planar realm within its gleaming crystalline surface; a nexus of many parallel worlds, a conduit linking alternate planes and universes with each other.
And something lives within the Source Stone as well. Of that I'm certain. A powerful life force emanates from the stone - probably from the inhabitants of the extra-planar realm.
That lizard creature Haedraline could probably tell you more, if she wanted to. But when I tried to speak to her she refused to answer my questions. I don't think she trusts me.
I need to see the Source Stone.
I would like to ask you some questions.
Me need see stone.
Me want ask questions.
Goodbye.

You should go speak to Master Ford. Maybe you can talk some sense into him and get him to give this all up.
Master Ford is messing with things he doesn't understand. Things like that Source Stone are best left to wizards, not professors and their students!
You'll have to see Master Ford about that. I don't know why anyone would want to see that thing, though. There's something evil about that stone - I can feel it!

I see even the slow witted are bitten by the curiosity bug. Seems the search for knowledge is a curse none of us can escape.

Normally Master Ford has the sense not to mess with magic, but he's fascinated by the Source Stone. That's him over there by the door.
I know it's a thing of great power - and great evil! I wish we had never found it. There's something alive inside - that's what Master Ford says.
You'd think that would make him more cautious, but he's behaving very strangely. It's like the stone has some strange hold over him.
I guess I shouldn't be surprised you've never heard of him.
They're with the Source Stone. Master Ford thinks they might help unlock the secrets of what's inside. Personally, there are some secrets I prefer not to know.
But this stone isn't like normal gems. We have no idea what we're getting into here, and I don't like this one bit.

Though the true origin of gloves of this type is unknown, those sold in Waterdeep often claim to be functional replicas of a pair of gloves once used by Halaster Blackcloak to assist him in making the notorious traps of Undermountain.
Greater Gloves of the Artificer
Gauntlet of Fury

This single wrought iron gauntlet was wrought by a former student of Laeral Silverhand Arunsun who joined the Red Wizards of Thay when he turned to evil.

An invisible but tangible field of force continuously surrounds the wearer, providing a bonus similar to a mage armor spell.

Once per day, the wearer can also cast a magic missile spell and a greater missile storm spell.
Gloves of Lightning

Once a personal "interrogation tool" of Rimardo Domine, an Overwizard of Luskan's Host Tower of the Arcane, these flexible leather gloves have since been circulated among powerful members of the pirate community.

The gloves are covered with small copper rivets.  The wearer may use the gloves to throw a sharp electric jolt at a nearby target.
Gloves of the Balanced Hands

Used as a training aid by the rangers of the Moonwood when tutoring aspiring students, these fine leather gloves allow the wearer to fight as if already trained in two-weapon fighting and ambidexterity.
Brooch of Shielding
A simple gold brooch, such as might be used to fasten a cloak.

This appears to be a piece of simple gold jewelry used to fasten a cloak or cape. In addition to this mundane task, the Brooch of Shielding can be activated with a touch to place an invisible field of force around the wearer, granting extra protection and immunity to magic missiles.

A common defensive tool among wizards, these brooches commonly bear the symbol of Mystra or Azuth.
Dove's Harp
A hand-held harp.

This item's original name has been lost, and its current name derives from Dove Falconhand, who owns such a harp.  These masterwork harps have from twenty to thirty-six strings.  When it is played, the harp's music can cure listeners and cast a warm light.
Austruth Harp
A small but well-crafted hand-held harp.

A wise and powerful bard in the Moonshaes named Falataer created the first of these instruments, using them to test and reward the students of his bardic college.  Others have since copied the designs, keeping the name Falataer gave them to honor him.
Ollamh Harp

A wise and powerful bard in the Moonshaes named Falataer created the first of these instruments, using them to test and reward the students of his bardic college. Others have since copied the designs, keeping the name Falataer gave them to honor him.

This masterwork harp can be played to cast mass charm, mass haste, and summon monster VI each once per day.
Janthra's Harp
By playing this masterwork harp the harpist can envelop all creatures within 10 feet of the harp in an invisibility sphere.
Deck of Hazards

This deck of cards appears to be designed for some kind of game of chance. The cards are ornately decorated and made of unusually thick paper that seems highly resistant to damage. A palpable aura of magic and danger surrounds them.

The mages of the Empire of Netheril once played the card game of Hazard for idle amusement, building decks of slightly magical cards to use in friendly competition against each other.

In the millennia since the fall of Netheril, however, the magic in the surviving decks has gradually steeped and intensified. Now, a Deck of Hazards produces many powerful effects both beneficial and baneful on those who take the risk of drawing cards from the deck.

An adventurer who is so fortunate -- or unfortunate, as the case may be -- to discover a Deck of Hazards may choose to draw one, two, or three cards. Once the decision has been made, however, it cannot be retracted. The specified number of cards will be drawn automatically, and then the deck will vanish forever.
Amulet of Undead Turning

These necklaces are occasionally distributed among the faithful by powerful temples, to protect them in holy missions against the undead. Necklaces of this type are usable only by non-evil clerics and paladins.  Amulets of this type are most commonly found in use among followers of Lathander, and these pendants often bear the symbol of the Morninglord.
Necklace of Fireballs
This appears to be nothing but a cheap medallion.

Once its true nature has been perceived, this necklace appears as a golden chain from which hang a number of golden spheres. The spheres are detachable by the wearer, who can easily hurl them over long distances.  When a sphere arrives at the end of its trajectory, it bursts into a magic fireball.

Different spheres do different amounts of damage.  The more damage a sphere deals, the bigger it is.

Many such devices have been created by wizards across Faerun, and this particular device bears no distinguishing marks to identify its creator.
Scarab of Protection
This device appears to be a silver medallion in the shape of a dung beetle. It gives off a faint magical aura.

This slender silver chain bears a medallion in the shape of a dung beetle.

The dung beetle was originally a holy creature associated with the Mulhorandi sun-god Ra due to its tendency to burrow a solar-disk-like circular hole in dung.  These creatures' likenesses were often used for the holy protective charms known as scarabs.  Since Ra's demise in the Orcgate Wars, his successor Horus-Re grants these totems their protective powers.
Luckstone
This thin chain bears a small pendant of roughly polished agate.

This slender chain bears a luckstone pendant of rough polished agate. Such stones come from the halfling homeland, Lurien.  "The luck of the hin" is said to have rubbed off on the rocks and grants the luck to the bearers of such trinkets.
Arvoreen's Amulet of Aid
This item is a three-inch-diameter gold disk with the holy symbol of Arvoreen inlaid in platinum. It grants the wearer the ability to cast aid six times.  It cannot be used by an evil creature.
Amulet of the Harpers

The mysterious semi-secret society called the Harpers makes these amulets  for their senior members. The amulets are fashioned from silver that has been magically treated to give it the hardness of steel and grant the wearer several magical protections.
Lesser Ice Necklace of the Ulutiun

Several of these necklaces of magically hardened and preserved ice were created by a half-mad sorcerer who wandered among the Ulutiun tribes of the Great Glacier.

The necklace mounts four transparent acorn-sized crystals.  The wearer can detach a crystal and hurl it at a distance.  When the crystal reaches the end of its trajectory, it explodes into a storm of ice storm.
Ring of Animal Friendship

Crafted of magically preserved twisted green twigs infused with the scent of edible berries, these rings are often employed by druids and rangers throughout the High Forest in pacifying the local wildlife.  Many have their twigs woven into subtle prayers to nature deities like Mielikki and Silvanus.
Ring of Hiding

This ring is actually a magic leather cord that ties around a finger.  It is tanned to be vaguely flesh-toned and is so subtle that it often goes unnoticed when worn.  Similarly, it allows the wearer to blend easily into the background to escape detection.

Though a common item among rogues and others who wish to go unnoticed, this item is rapidly becoming standard equipment among the Night Masks, according to the Westgate city watch.
Ring of Improved Evasion

This ring continually grants the wearer extreme nimbleness, allowing her to avoid damage as if she had the improved evasion ability.

These rings have been used as training tools among the Red Wizards in an effort to lower the mortality rate among apprentice battle mages.
Ring of Force Shield

Made by the Harpell clan of wizards in Longsaddle, these simple iron bands generate a large shield-sized invisible wall of force that stays with the ring and can be wielded by the wearer as if it were a normal shield. This special creation, since it can be activated and deactivated at will, has no armor check penalty or arcane spell failure chance.
Ring of Freedom of Movement
This gold ring allows the wearer to act as if continually under the effect of a freedom of movement spell.  The name of Shaundakul is inscribed in flowing script on the inside of the band.
Aribeth's Ring
Once the family heirloom of an elven paladin of Tyr, this protective ring was lost with the fall of its owner in combat.
Bone Ring

Crafted by clerics of Myrkul, these rings are carved from stone or ivory as often as from bone, but are never made of metal. The rings grant their wearer immunity to energy drain and ability drain attacks.
Commander's Ring
The war wizards of Cormyr forge these protective rings for use by the Cormyrian military. With the proper command word, a commander's ring can also cast the useful spells of knock and light.
Ring of Disease Immunity

The wearers of these rings are immune to all types of infections and diseases.

Lacksun Zollan, a Cormyrian paladin of Ilmater, has travelled much of Faerun granting such rings to those he deems to be victims of priests of Talona.  As he has become fond of saying, he plans to break Talona's work "one finger at a time."
Ring of Might
These rings are forged by clerics of Tyr to assist adherents. The wearer of such a ring of might gains great prowess at unarmed combat.
Ring of Nine Lives
This ancient Netherese ring is made of ivory and carved to resemble a snarling cat's face on one end.  It allows the wearer to cast a heal spell up to nine times.
Purple Dragon Ring

These rings are brass and engraved with the purple dragon symbol of the Obarskyr royal family. The Purple Dragons use these rings to protect the royal family from assassination attempts by poison.  Over 4,000 of these rings have been made.  Rings with similar functions are in common circulation, created for nobles or merchants fearing poison.
Ring of Spell Battle

This potent Netherese ring is typically made of gold and set with small spheres of silver. The ring aids the wearer in identifying spells being cast nearby. In the event of unwanted spell effects, the ring also allows the wearer to cast dispel magic once per day.
Bowl of Commanding Water Elementals
This large bowl is fashioned out of a pale blue semiprecious stone. It seems fairly fragile.

This large bowl is fashioned out of pale blue lapis lazuli, and the rim of the bowl is etched with a smooth, flowing script spelling out prayers to Istishia. When filled with water, a water elemental will be summoned to serve the caster.

Who you be again?

Come on over here and get your equipment.
Hello there, <FirstName>. Come to get yourself some supplies from old Olgerd, have you? Good idea. We can't have you wandering about the streets naked. Might give the Academy a bad name.

The city guard are already having enough trouble maintaining control as it is. Plague bodies piled a dozen deep in the gutters, the Wailing Death running unchecked through the districts... horrible, I say!
But you've heard all this before, I'm sure. And you need to get some equipment so you can continue your training. I guess it's time you learned how to access your inventory. Ready?
The top section of the inventory shows equipped items. There are slots for your weapon, shield, armor, belts, capes, rings and other items.
The bottom section of your inventory shows items stored in your backpack. Notice the six tabs on the right hand side. Each tab opens up another page in your backpack's inventory.
To equip items, simply left-click and hold while dragging them to the appropriate section at the top of your inventory page. Or, you can right-click on an item and choose "Equip" from the menu.
If you right-click on an item in your inventory, you will see a menu with an "Examine" option at the top. Selecting this will allow you to learn more about the object.
When you examine magical items, the game will automatically check your Lore skill. If your skill is high enough, you will get a complete description of the properties and abilities of the object.
This might be a good time to teach you how to use stores in the game. I have some items here you might want to purchase. Since you're part of the Academy you get a special discount rate.
Are you interested in seeing my store? I'll give you a quick tutorial in how they work, too.
Before we enter the store, let me explain how it works. This is important, you're going to be using stores quite a bit during your adventures.
Fair enough. Still, let me explain how the stores work - you're going to need them at some time during your adventures.
At the top of the store menu you'll see different tabs for the different types of equipment. Click on a tab and it will bring up the first page of the store menu with that type of equipment.

There are arrow buttons in the upper corners of the store menu for scrolling through the different inventory pages. On each page, passing the cursor over an item will display the name and cost at the bottom of the menu.
To buy something simply click and drag it from the store menu to your own inventory. This will purchase the item and automatically deduct the gold from your total.
Selling items works the same way. Just click and drag an item from your inventory to the store menu and the item will be sold.

To identify an item just click on the EXAMINE icon in the bottom left of the store menu then click on the item you need identified. This will bring up a menu with a picture of the item and an IDENTIFY button on the left.
Click the IDENTIFY button and a confirmation box will appear detailing the cost of the service.
To leave the store at anytime simply click your mouse on the X in the top right corner of the store menu.
That's about it as far as stores go. So, are you interested in seeing my inventory now?
Great - I'm sure you'll find my prices most reasonable. When we're done you'll find the door leading out of this room is unlocked.
As long as you're here at the Academy you're welcome to come back to buy any equipment you need. Now - let's take a look at my wares.
Okay, you must be eager to get on with your adventures. You'll find the door to the south is unlocked now.
Goodbye, then. Remember - you're always welcome to come back and view the Menagerie anytime you want. I always enjoy it when people take an interest in my little beasties.
Welcome back, <FirstName>. Have you come to take a look at the Menagerie, or is there something else I can do for you?
Certainly. As long as you're here at the Academy you're free to view the Menagerie anytime you want. Don't worry, the monsters in there can't hurt you.
Ask your questions, <FullName>, and I'll do my best to answer.
I bet you do, my slow witted friend. Hopefully I can explain them so you can understand.
You have to stop the attackers from getting the Waterdhavian creatures!
You actually want to know something about me? That's a twist. Most people just want to see the creatures in the Menagerie. They're far more interesting than I am.
When I was young I always knew I wanted to work with animals, but I didn't really want to live the life of a druid or a ranger. I didn't relish the idea of living out in the wild all by myself.

I worked for a while at the zoo in Neverwinter, tending the animals and such. That lead to an apprenticeship here at the Academy under the former Keeper of Exotic Creatures. When she retired I took over the job of running the Menagerie.
The Wailing Death is a grim topic, <FirstName>. Thousands have fallen to the illness, and not even the clerics can do anything about it.
Not one of the creatures in the Menagerie showed a single sign of the plague. Can't figure it out, but I'm grateful. I'd feel responsible if one of my beasties took sick.
I know there's a rumor going around the barracks about some strange creatures from Waterdeep being brought here to concoct a cure, but I don't believe it.
Although I have to admit, if you wanted to keep the arrival of any strange creatures secret you wouldn't store them in the Menagerie. That would be the first place people would think to look.
Sure, I can tell you again.
Sure, I don't mind repeating myself.
Sure, this is important. I don't mind going over it again.
Something strange about this plague, though. It infects humans, dwarves, elves - all the races, in fact - but it doesn't seem to affect animals. That's very unusual.
Well then, I guess we don't need to go over it, do we?
Okay, I'm not one to go prattling on when the listener already knows what I'm saying. So, you want to see my inventory now?
Go ahead and do that now if you want. It won't interrupt our conversation.

If your Lore skill is too low to properly identify an item, you will not receive the fully detailed description when you examine it, and you cannot use or equip an item until it is identified. Stores can identify these items for you for a fee.
The Identify spell will temporarily increase your Lore skill to raise your chances of identifying items when you examine them. Do you understand what I have said about examining items?
Sure.
Not interested.
May I ask you some questions?
Can me ask you stuff?
What can you tell me about the Wailing Death?
Do you know anything about a cure for the plague?
Goodbye.
What you know 'bout Wailing Death?
What you know 'bout plague cure?
Tell me about Lady Aribeth.
You talk 'bout Aribeth, kay?
Where can I go to complete my training?
Where me go for finish me training?

Yes.
No.

Hey, there. You're one of the students here at the Academy, aren't you? <FirstName>, unless I'm mistaken.
I'm Berna, an instructor here at the Academy. If you like I can give you a quick tutorial on how to use your map and journal.
Back again, <FirstName>? You want me to go over the tutorial on how to use your map and journal?
We're under attack! We have to slay the invaders!
Of course. We instructors are here to give guidance to the students, after all. How else will you complete your training?
Goodbye, <FirstName>.
I know the quarantine of the city has done little to stop the affliction from spreading, though it has bred mistrust and fear among the people.
Lady Aribeth does her best to keep the peace, but the rumors are beginning to fly. People suspect some dark evil is behind the Wailing Death.
Soon the panic may lead to open rebellion. I pray we of the Academy are not forced into battle against the citizens of Neverwinter. They are the very people we are supposed to protect!
So you have heard the rumors as well? You should focus on your studies and not idle gossip.
Lady Aribeth is no doubt seeking a cure, but there has been no official word. And spreading rumors about a cure being stored here at the Academy is dangerous.
It draws unwanted attention. The people are desperate for a cure - so desperate they might even attack the Academy itself if they feel we have one.
Lady Aribeth de Tylmarande is a Paladin of Tyr. She may be young, but she has already proven her courage and her devotion to both Neverwinter and Tyr.
Lord Nasher Alagondar himself has given Lady Aribeth the task of saving Neverwinter from the Wailing Death.
She's actually here at the Academy right now, in the south assembly hall. Once you've finished your training you can go to meet her.
Just head through the exit in the southwest corner of this room. The Academy training rooms are all in the hallway beyond.
Once you finish your training you can go meet Aribeth in the south assembly hall.
To use your journal, simply left-click on the Journal box beneath your character portrait or press the "J" key on your keyboard. Go ahead and do that now... it won't end our conversation.
This brings up your journal entries for the current chapter. Right now you should see two quests in your journal: "Academy Training" and "Speaking to Berna."
Well, if you change your mind I'll be right here to help you out. Is there anything else I can do for you?
Go ahead and click on the "Speaking to Berna" entry to get the detailed description of that entry. You can click on an entry to bring up more details at any time.
Sure, I'll go over it one more time.
Okay, first make sure your journal is closed. Now, to use your map, left-click the MAP box beneath your character portrait or press "M" on your keyboard. The top of the map is always north.
Go ahead and do that now. Your location on the map is marked by an arrow, and the arrow points in the direction you are facing. Do you understand so far?
I'll go over it again.
The arrow keys on the top of the map let you zoom in or out. Maps will fill in as you explore an area. You can leave the map up to help guide you as you are adventuring.
You will also see that there are small pins tacked onto the map. These are your map notes; they mark important locations in an area. Simply move your mouse over one of the pins to read the notes.
You can add your own map notes by clicking the PIN in the upper left corner of the map screen, then clicking the area on the map where you wish to add the note.
That's it as far as the map and journal go. You can close your map now if you want. Just click the MAP icon below your character sheet or hit "M" on your keyboard.
I'll go over it one more time for you.
Come over here if you want to learn about your map and journal.
Can I ask you some questions?

Sorry, recruit. The assembly chamber is reserved for Academy students who have completed their training. Lady Aribeth is in there granting blessings to all the graduates.
You can't go in until you finish your training.
You have to report to Herban to finish your combat training. Hurry up, he doesn't like to be kept waiting. Just go back down this hall and take the second door on your left.
You better go speak to Jaroo - he's the one who trains all you mage types. Just go back down this hall to the third door on your right.
You have to go to the temple and speak to Elynwyd to finish your training. Just head back down this hallway and take the first door on your left.
Judging by those shifty eyes, I think you need to speak to Ketta in the espionage room to complete your training. Just go back down this hall and take the first door on your right.

If you're looking to learn the ways of espionage and thieves, head back down this hall and take the first door on your right. If you want to study a bit about spellcasting, keep going to the third door on your right.

I guess congratulations are in order. You've passed the combat trial and completed your Basic Training. Your days at the Academy are finally over.
Well done. I need to talk to you.
If you hurry you can join the other Academy graduates in the south assembly hall. Lady Aribeth is there bestowing blessings on everyone who has completed Basic Training.
So long then.

Keep in mind this is only the final stage of everything you have learned while you have been here at the Academy. This is a mere formality - you've already proven yourself worthy of going out into the world.
Oh, come on. Surely you knew that Lady Aribeth de Tylmarande, the famous Elven paladin of Tyr, was here at the Academy. Everybody's talking about it.
I hope I get a chance to meet her when my shift is over.
Sorry, not while I'm on duty. Herban will bust my ass down three ranks if he catches me socializing at my post. Besides, I thought you'd be more interested in celebrating the end of your tour.
You need to speak to Herban first. He's in charge here.
So Herban sent you over for your combat trial, did he? Well, my name is Dendy. I specialize in melee weapon combat. Are you ready to begin the final test?
Don't worry, there's nothing to it. You and I are going to spar. I'll be in parry mode the whole time, trying to deflect your attacks. All you have to do is hit me once to pass the test.
Or, if you prefer, all you have to do is use your weapon to destroy the target dummy next to me. The choice is up to you, either attack me or the dummy.
Then you should go talk to Hewwet on the other side of the room. He's the expert with ranged and missile weapons. I'm only certified to test you in melee weapons.
Sorry, but I can't. Herban can be a real hard-ass, and I don't want to get into trouble for chatting while I'm on duty. If you're not here to take the combat test I really can't talk to you.
Since I'm not hostile, you'll have to right-click on me then select the attack icon from the menu if you want to attack me. You can begin whenever you're ready.
Well done, but you should continue your training elsewhere.
Go and talk to Hewwet to continue your test.
You've passed the combat tests, but your training here at the Academy isn't over yet.

Go and talk to Hewwet to continue your test.

Can't you see I'm practicing my drills? The Academy might go easy on a <class> like you, but those of us training under Herban can't afford to waste our time chatting!
Back again? I'm pretty busy here - what do you want this time?
Look, I'm not trying to be rude. It's just that Herban doesn't like us taking breaks from our drills. It's a sign of weakness!
Okay, but make it quick. I need to finish my drills so I can attend the graduation ceremonies. I don't want to miss my chance to meet Lady Aribeth.
Then I'll get back to my drills.
Get on with it then. The sooner you ask, the sooner I can get back to my training.
Lady Aribeth represents everything the Academy stands for: skill and bravery and honor! She's the reason I joined the Academy in the first place.
She's young, but she's already proven her heroism a dozen times over. That's why Lord Nasher put her in charge of dealing with the plague.
It's not for the faint of heart, that's for sure! Rise at dawn, march for an hour and then an hour of drills. And that's just before breakfast!
Herban doesn't stand for weakness or failure. He drives the recruits hard, but these are tough times. Anyone who can't take it probably shouldn't be training at the Academy anyway.
The training is tough, but the rewards are worth it. Lady Aribeth herself is even here to congratulate the graduating recruits. The chance to meet her in person is inspiration enough for me.
I try not to think about it, to tell you the truth. I need to stay focused on my training. But since you brought it up, there's one thing I don't understand about the Wailing Death.
There's something unnatural about this plague, though it seems nobody wants to admit it. I guess they're afraid of panic in the streets. But you can't deny the facts.
I heard about Blackstaff and his cure. I don't like putting my faith in wizards, but I heard Lady Aribeth trusts him. She's at the Academy, you know. I hope I get a chance to meet her.
Where did it come from? Neverwinter's the only city that seems to be suffering. And why can't the priests cure it?
Defend the Waterdhavian creatures! Don't let them be taken!
You can't be serious, everybody knows fighting between recruits will get you kicked out of the Academy! Take your blustering threats somewhere else. I've got to get back to my drills.

Are you kidding me? This is Lady Aribeth de Tylmarande! Defender of Tyr's faith, Champion of Neverwinter! She's a living legend.

Terrible thing, isn't it? They've got the entire city under quarantine, but every day there are more bodies in the street. Terrible.

I heard something about creatures being brought to the Academy from Waterdeep to make a cure. I just hope it's true. That's probably why Lady Aribeth is here today. I hope she takes the time to tour the barracks, I'd love to meet her.

Besides, Aribeth may be attractive and all but I'm more interested in a woman's inner beauty. Physical looks only go so deep - I'm more interested in a woman with character. Like you.

I understand. The training here at the Academy isn't easy. We recruits don't have a lot of free time for things like relationships. Still, you can't blame a guy for trying. Is there something else you need?
I find that hard to believe - a fascinating woman like you without a man in her life.
I'm sorry. I didn't mean to be rude. I was just... I mean, I just wanted to know if you were seeing anyone. I figured a fascinating woman like you probably already has a boyfriend, is all.
I hope I'm not being too forward but there's the big feast tonight in honor of all the Academy graduates. If you're not going with anyone, maybe we could go together.
Great! I'm looking forward to it. Listen, I better get back to my drills. If I don't finish Herban might not let me go to the feast. Unless there was something else you needed?
I guess I'll see you later tonight, then. I'm looking forward to it.
Wow! That was harsh! Okay, I get the message loud and clear. You're not interested. Thanks for crushing my spirit and will to live.
I should really get back to me drills. Excuse me.
I should have known. That's okay - it's kind of late notice. Is there something else I can do for you?
Is there something else I can help you with?
And how's your training going? If you're half as talented as you are beautiful, the Academy must be a snap for you.
And how's your training going? A woman as obviously talented as you must just be breezing through the training.
We're under attack! We have to protect the Waterdhavian creatures!
You made it pretty clear how you feel about me. We've got nothing more to say to each other.
So do I. I'm really looking forward to it. Is there something else I can do for you, then?
I want to try the combat drills, Sir!

Sir! Please repeat, Sir!
Yeah, yeah. I've got it. No need to shout and holler.

I already know everything I need to about combat!

Not interested.
Sir! I wish to hear your combat tutorial, Sir!
Sir! Me want hear you tutorial!
Get your ass over here now, recruit!
It's about time you showed up, <FirstName>! My name is Herban, but as far as your worthless hide is concerned you can just call me "Sir!"
Whenever you want to use a feat or special attack on an enemy, right-click on your opponent to bring up the menu. Then, left-click on the Special Attack icon in the lower right corner of the menu.
This opens up a second menu with any feats or special attacks you might have. Just left-click on the attack or feat you want to use.
When parrying, you do not attack but you are able to make an opposed check to deflect or dodge any incoming attacks that would otherwise hit you.
Each round, you can parry one successful enemy attack for each attack you would normally get. If your roll succeeds by ten or greater, you will make a free counterattack at no penalty.

You aren't really a fighter type so you aren't required to participate in combat drills. They are open to anyone, however, and if you pass the combat test it will complete your basic training, but I'd recommend you go study under your specialized trainer instead.
I think you might be more suited to taking on one of the other tests to complete your training, but if you really want to tackle the combat trials you have that right, recruit!
I figured as much. You're no warrior. Go test your skills on one of the other tests and trials here at the Academy! You're dismissed, recruit!
It's my job to teach you raw recruits some tips on combat technique so you maggots don't get gutted out there in the real world!
Well, recruit, don't just stand there with that dopey expression on your face! What's it going to be? Are you ready to begin your combat training or aren't you?
Wrong answer, recruit! Everybody needs to learn how to handle themselves in a fight! So you better get ready for this training in a hurry!
Maybe you think you don't need this kind of training, is that it? When you're staring down the point of some orc's crooked blade you'll wish you hadn't been such a smart ass!
Get out of here and don't come back until you're ready to learn, recruit!
You address me as "Sir" when you open your mouth, maggot! If this plague hadn't made us so desperate for recruits, I'd boot your worthless ass out of here for that type of attitude!
But I'm stuck with you and I don't have time to break your spirit and teach you proper respect and discipline. We don't have to like each other, but you will listen to what I have to say!
This information might save your life sometime, recruit, so listen up:
That's what I like to hear, recruit! With that attitude you might actually make something of yourself in this world!
On the special attacks menu, you will also see the Parry icon located at the very top in the 12 o'clock position. Left-click on this icon whenever you want to enter parry mode.

Go speak to my assistants. Corporal Dendy at the southeast end of the room can test you in melee weapons. Then, for your test in ranged combat and missile weapons, speak to Corporal Hewwet over near the west wall.
Since you're a paladin I better show you how to use your special abilities. Just right-click on yourself to bring up the menu, then left-click on the special abilities icon on the left of the menu.
This will bring up the menu to access all your class-specific special abilities. Left-click on an ability to activate it or bring up a menu of class-specific abilities. That clear?
I see you're a barbarian. I better show you how to use your rage ability. Just right-click on yourself to bring up the menu, then left-click on the special abilities icon on the left of the menu.
This will bring up the menu to access all your class-specific special abilities. Left-click on the rage icon to activate your special ability. That clear, recruit?
You're a ranger, so you automatically get the dual-wield feat. As long as you wear only light armor you can use two weapons as if you had the ambidexterity and two-weapon fighting feats.
Remember, you lose your special dual-wield abilities if you wear medium or heavy armor. That clear, recruit?
You're a monk, so I better show you how to use your flurry of blows special ability.
Right-click on your target to bring up the menu, then left-click on the special attacks icon on the lower right of the menu to bring up your special attack menu. From there click the upper left icon.
This brings up the "More Special Attacks" menu. Finally, left-click on the Flurry of Blows icon located on the left of the menu. That clear, recruit?
I've done my part, the rest is up to you, recruit. Time to prove yourself by facing one of the Academy's combat tests.
Back again, recruit? What do you want this time? And you better address me as "Sir" or this conversation is over!
Then quit bothering me! I don't have time to be holding the hand of every kid who comes through the Academy. We're here to train you maggots, not babysit you!
Oh, you recruits are always full of questions, aren't you? Was the plague really started by an enemy of Neverwinter, Sir? Are the Waterdhavian creatures really here at the Academy, Sir?

Well, you better forget about those questions and focus on the here and now, recruit! Your ass belongs to the Academy until you step out those doors! The outside world is nothing to you. Do you hear me? NOTHING!
You've passed the combat trials, recruit. There's nothing more we can teach you here. You've completed your Basic Training - time to reap the rewards!
Just head out into the hall and go to the south end. The guard there will let you into the assembly hall with the rest of the graduating recruits.
Damn it, recruit! Go find those Waterdhavian creatures and protect them!
You follow me so far, recruit?
You got a real attitude problem, <boy/girl>! But your smart mouth isn't going to be my problem much longer! So listen up and let's get this lesson over with!
Are you trying to tell me you haven't heard one damn word I've said, recruit? This is for your benefit, maggot, so listen up this time!
Are we clear so far, recruit?
When a giant is ripping your lips off for talking back, recruit, just remember that somewhere I'll be smiling! Now quit goofing off and stay sharp!
What's the matter, recruit? You got nothing between your ears to stop my words from going in one side and out the other? Pay attention this time, maggot!
Is this a joke, <boy/girl>? Or do you just love the sound of my soothing voice? Listen close this time, recruit!
You know what, funny <boy/girl>? You ain't my problem anymore!
You think that's funny, recruit? Well, I left my sense of humor dangling on the point of a blood encrusted Luskan spear thirty years ago, so don't waste your jokes on me!
Get out of my face, recruit! I'm sick of your wiseass ways!
To return to normal combat mode, simply left-click on your foe. Have you got that figured out, recruit? Can we move on to the next lesson?
Your weapon isn't just for killing, recruit. Sometimes it has other uses, like opening a chest or locked door.
If you find a lock you can't get past, right-click on the door or chest, then select the "Bash" icon from the menu. You can even do this with missile weapons.
The stronger you are, the easier it is to bash open a lock. Just remember that not all locks can be opened by force.
Are you really this stupid, recruit, or are you just trying to make my life a living hell? Listen up and I'll go over it again!
If I don't shout, recruit, it might not get through that thick layer of dung covering your brain! Now listen up for the next lesson!
Is that so, recruit? For the sake of your worthless hide, I hope that's true.
But I'm going to give you one last chance to change your mind and listen to my tutorial on basic combat techniques.
You've done the combat drills, recruit! But you're a <class>, not a soldier! There's nothing more we can teach you here.
If you want to graduate from the Academy you'll have to prove yourself by completing the <class> challenge.
Lady Aribeth?

If you hurry you can join the other Academy graduates in the south assembly hall. Lady Aribeth is there bestowing blessings on everyone who has completed Basic Training.
Goodbye.

Keep in mind this is only the final stage of everything you have learned while you have been here at the Academy. This is a mere formality, you've already proven yourself worthy of going out into the world.
You're kidding, right? Everyone knows that Lady Aribeth de Tylmarande, the famous Elven paladin of Tyr, is here at the Academy. Everybody's talking about it.
I hope I get a chance to meet her when my shift is over.

Sorry, not while I'm on duty. Herban has rules against us chatting at our posts. He wants us to stay focused on our work. Besides, I thought you'd be more interested in celebrating the end of your tour.
You need to speak to Herban first. He's in charge here.
So Herban sent you over for your combat trial, did he? Well, my name is Hewwet. I specialize in ranged and missile weapon combat. Are you ready to begin the final test?
Don't worry, there's nothing to it. All you have to do is hit the target at the end of the hall with a missile weapon. You can grab a missile weapon from the weapon rack here beside me.
Fire away whenever you're ready. I'll let you know if you hit the target.
Then you should go talk to Dendy on the other side of the room. He's the expert with melee weapons. I'm only certified to test you in missile and ranged weapons.
Sorry, but I can't. Herban demoted the last guy caught socializing at his post. Harsh but fair, I say. If you're not here to take the combat test I really can't talk to you.
That shot was taken too close to the target. It doesn't count. Move back and try again.
Not bad. But since you are a <class>, you should be training elsewhere.
You've completed my part of the test. Go speak with Dendy for the second part.
You've passed the combat tests, but your training here at the Academy isn't over yet.
You have to go finish the <class> challenge before they'll let you graduate. I can't do anything more for you here.
Nice Shot. You've completed my part of the test. Go speak with Dendy for the second part.

Normally I object to flattery, but only a fool dismisses compliments from a beautiful woman.

Uh... me got date already. Sorry, Chandra.
Hello there. You are <FirstName>, aren't you? We were in the same arcane theory class I believe. My name is Chandra.
I do not recognize you from any of my classes. You must be new here at the Academy. Unless... of course, how could I have not noticed? You are a <class>, not a mage.
No wonder your face is not familiar; I highly doubt the Academy has us following the same curriculum. Allow me to introduce myself. My name is Chandra.
Hello again, <FirstName>. Is there something I can do for you?
<FullName>? Oh yes, I have a friend who recently enrolled here at the Academy. He is also a <class>. I believe he has mentioned your name to me before.
From what I hear, <FirstName>, your training at the Academy is almost done. You have only to prove yourself in the final <class> challenge and you will be ready for graduation.
I've heard your study here at the Academy is almost complete, <FirstName>. You must be looking forward to graduating.
I envy you. I hear Lady Aribeth herself is here to hand out personal blessings to all the graduates in the south assembly hall. I hope she returns for my own graduation. I would love to meet her.
I suppose I will resume my studies then. Jaroo has given me a number of incantations to prepare.
I do apologize. There must be someone else who looks like you here at the Academy.
Uh... yes. I already recognized you, remember?
Certainly. Jaroo always says that asking questions is the most important step in seeking answers.
Lady Aribeth de Tylmarande is an inspiration to all the citizens of Neverwinter, especially those of us here at the Academy.
She is everything I wish to be, intelligent, powerful and beautiful. Someday I hope to be as loved and respected as she, though some might say that is a foolish and silly dream.
I could ask for no finer instructor than Jaroo. He is both patient and well versed in the arcane arts.
To be sure the lessons are difficult and the workload is often great. I have spent many nights burning countless candles as I study my tomes.
But success comes to those who persevere. One need only look to Lady Aribeth to see a shining example of that. I do hope I get a chance to meet her before she leaves.
The work is difficult, but Jaroo is quick to aid any who stumble in their pursuit of the ancient knowledge. He is a fine instructor.
You flatter me, <FirstName>. Most people laugh at me when I dare compare myself to Lady Aribeth, even though we are both of noble blood.
Perhaps someday I will be as famous as she, but I fear that day is a long way off. I shall thank you for the compliment nevertheless. Is there something else you wish to know?
You are kind not to scoff at my dream. Often men who are as handsome as you harbor a bitter, mean spirit to compensate. I am glad to see you are of a gentle, compassionate nature.
I know little enough about it. My family were nobles of the Blacklake district and the Wailing Death has yet to touch that section of the city, thanks to the quarantine.
Perhaps they are right in their suspicions of the plague's origins, but it is not right to blame all wizards for this terrible tragedy. In their ignorance they judge us when they do not even know us.
Thankfully, Lady Aribeth herself is not prejudiced against wizards, or she may have refused Blackstaff's offer of aid. I hope I get a chance to meet her before she leaves the Academy.
Hello again, <FirstName>. I hope you haven't changed your mind about our date tonight.
I do know that there are those who blame the plague on foul necromancy, even here in the Academy. Their eyes burn with hatred whenever they look upon my mage's cloak.
You are kind not to scoff at my words. The woman in your life is very lucky... or dare I believe one of such noble and gentle spirit is still unattached?
You are kind not to scoff at my words. I am ashamed to admit this, but I assumed by your rough appearance that you were something of a beast. But I see now you have a true and gentle heart.
I understand. Many men, even other mages, are intimidated by a woman who commands the powers of magic. Is there something else you need, then?
That is a shame. In these troubled times no one should be alone - particularly a man as kind and understanding as you obviously are.
Forgive me, I am not trying to pry. But in these troubled times no one should be alone - particularly a man as kind and understanding as you obviously are.

We might exchange coy flirtations all day, <FirstName>, but I am a woman who prefers action. There is a feast tonight in honor of the Academy graduates. Perhaps you would accompany me to the festival?
As would I. Jaroo wants me to prepare these cantrips for tomorrow, I should resume my studies so I am free for tonight. Unless there was something else you needed?
I shall see you later tonight then. I hear the graduation feast is spectacular, I am looking forward to our evening together.
I see. I thought there was a mutual attraction between us. Obviously I was mistaken. Rest assured I will trouble you no longer with such foolishness.
Excuse me now, please. I really must return to my studies. I have a number of cantrips to master before the morrow.
I am not surprised. As they say, the good men are all taken. Rest assured there are no hard feelings. Is there something else I can do for you?
Is there something else I can help you with?
And how is your training going? If you are half as talented as you are handsome you must surely be at the head of all your classes.
And how is your training going? Surely a man as talented as you must have no difficulty mastering all the challenges the Academy presents.
We have to protect the Waterdhavian creatures!
You left little doubt as to how you feel about me. I have nothing further to say to you.
Some men, even other mages, are intimidated by a woman who wields powerful magic. I am glad to learn you are not so insecure. Is there something else I can do for you, then?
I hope the rumors are true. If Khelben Arunsun really has discovered a cure, then perhaps those who blame the plague on sorcery will begin to treat us mages with respect instead of contempt and fear.
I would like to receive a lesson in casting spells.
Me want learn how cast spells.
I would like to ask you some questions.
Me want ask you questions.
I am ready for the Mage's Challenge.
Me ready for Mage Challenge.
Goodbye.

Simple. Go on.

Whoa - me no follow. You say again, 'kay?
Okay. What else?
Sorry, but could you go over that one more time?
Me sorry, but mabye you be say that again, 'kay?
I don't need a final tutorial. I'm ready for the Mage's Challenge now.
Me not need final tutorial - me want do Mage Challenge now.
Ready.
Forget about me - go protect the Waterdhavian creatures!
Come speak to me.

Hey there, <FullName>, welcome to my little corner of the Academy. I'm Jaroo, resident Master of the Arcane. It's more a ceremonial title than anything else. I'm really just your run-of-the-mill wizard.
No doubt you have come here to complete your training. Well, you've come to the right place. Nobody at this institution knows more about teaching you apprentices magic than me.
Look, <FirstName>, I'm not trying to be rude, but are you sure you're in the right place? My expertise is in mage and sorcerer spells, and you can't cast either type.
If you want, I guess I can give you a lesson in casting spells, but it won't bring you any closer to completing your training at the Academy. Or do you need something else?
Ah, <FirstName>, I didn't expect you to come back. What can I do for you?
Well, <FirstName>, have you decided to take the Mage's Challenge? It's the final step in your training here at the Academy, after all.
Good luck to you, <FirstName>. I don't know what your future holds, but I sense you are destined for great things.
Your training is done, <FirstName>. You should go to the south assembly hall to receive a blessing and congratulations from Lady Aribeth.
Since you're a wizard, I'll start by showing you how to prepare spells.
Since you're not a wizard you don't need to learn how to prepare spells. If you want I can still show you how it's done, but you won't need to learn it.
To prepare a spell, you have to access your spellbooks. Don't do this now or you'll break out of dialog and have to start over. Just listen to my instructions and you can try it later.
This will bring up your spellbook menu. On the left side you will see all the spells in your spellbook. On the right side, you will see the spells you currently have prepared.
Click and drag the spells you want to prepare from your spellbook over to your prepared spells page. Don't forget that you'll have to rest before the spells are prepared.
Okay, I guess we can move right on to the lessons about resting.

It's very important for a spellcaster to remember to rest. Resting is how you replenish your spells. To rest, simply click the Rest icon below your character portrait. It's the one that looks like a closed eyelash.
Okay, I guess we'll start with the basics. Bards and sorcerers don't have to prepare spells to cast them, but wizards can only cast spells they've prepared beforehand.
Whenever you rest, your spells will replenish themselves. Lower level spells replenish first and more quickly; higher level spells take longer.
If you have the spells loaded into your quickbar, you'll see their icons highlight as they get refreshed. Remember to rest often, but don't forget that you can't rest while in combat.

During your adventures, you will find scrolls with spells you haven't learned. Wizards can scribe new spells from scrolls into their spellbooks, but sorcerers and bards can only learn new spells when they increase in level.

To add a new spell to your spellbook, simply open your inventory and spellbook at the same time. Then, drag the scroll from your inventory to your spellbook. Remember that scribing a spell from a scroll like this will destroy the scroll.
That's it. The basics of spell casting in a nutshell. So, <FirstName>, you ready to face the Mage's Challenge? It's the last step in completing your arcane training here at the Academy.
That's all I can teach you about casting spells, <FirstName>, though I don't see what use the knowledge of arcane magic will be to you. Is there something else I can do for you?
The test is a simple one, <FirstName>. See the statue in the center of the room? All you have to do is destroy it using a spell and the challenge will be complete.

To help you in this task, there are two scrolls in the chest against the north wall. You can scribe these scrolls to your spellbook or right-click on the scrolls and select the Use Item icon from the menu to cast the spell right from the scroll.
The best way to actually cast your spells is by using the quickbar. Remember: you have two extra quickbars that can be accessed using the "SHIFT" and "CTRL" keys.
To load a spell onto your quickbar, simply open your spellbook, then click and drag the spell to the desired slot on one of your quickbars. The spell can now be cast with a single keystroke.
Non-targeted spells will cast automatically after you select them using the quickbar, but many spells require a target, be it a creature, an object or even a spot on the ground.
After selecting a targeting spell using the quickbar, your cursor will change to display the spell icon. To then cast the spell, simply left-click with your cursor on the target.
Come speak to me when you finish the test. I'll be waiting right here.
Is something wrong, <FirstName>? I see you haven't finished the Mage's Challenge. Do you need me to go over it one more time?
Okay, I'll do my best. Fire away.
One thing I can tell you is not to believe unfounded rumors. Those who claim the plague was caused intentionally by some unknown enemy of Neverwinter are only adding to the panic.
Nobody knows where the Wailing Death came from, just as nobody knows how to stop it from spreading. And until now there hasn't been any prayer or potion that can cure it.
But I think Lady Aribeth is headed in the right direction now. She's a smart one, and I think Lord Nasher made the right choice putting her in charge of dealing with this plague.

I shouldn't say anything, but I suppose the information is common knowledge among the students by now. Khelben Arunsun, the most famous mage this side of Elminster himself, discovered a cure for the Wailing Death.
Waterdeep helped us out by capturing the monsters necessary to concoct the cure and they sent them here to the Academy for safekeeping. That's the real reason Lady Aribeth is here, I suspect.

Well, I've never actually met her myself. I know she's an Elven paladin in the service of Tyr, and I know she's the one in charge of keeping order in Neverwinter and finding a cure for the Wailing Death.

And, of course, everybody knows she's here giving blessings to those who have finished their Academy training. Students have been piling into the south assembly hall since early this morning just to meet her.
Leave it to a mage to come up with a cure when all the priests and healers couldn't, right? Old Blackstaff figured out that combining the proper reagents would make an elixir to save us all.
Sure, we don't want you to miss out on this. It's important stuff.
Consider this a final tutorial on casting spells before you face the Mage's Challenge. Are you ready to begin?
Really? Well - if you're ready then I guess we can begin.
Congratulations, you have shown great control of your magical abilities. Speak to me before you leave.
To bring up your spellbook menu, press the "B" key or left-click on the SPELLBOOK button below your character portrait.
Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt.

Can't you see that I'm in the middle of training? The Academy might go easy on a <class> like you, but those of us wishing to master the arcane cannot afford to waste our days chatting.
You again? Can you not see I am in the middle of my training? What is it you want this time?
This spell demands my full attention and I cannot afford these constant interruptions!
(Sigh) Master Jaroo often warns me about the perils of prolonged casting. Perhaps a short break would be good for me. Perhaps it will even give me a chance to meet Lady Aribeth.
Then I shall resume my perusal of these rather obscure and difficult texts.
Very well. Perhaps if I answer your questions you will stop pestering me.
She is a powerful and influential figure within the city. Lady Aribeth has been given the task of finding a cure for the plague by Lord Nasher himself.
Lady Aribeth could be a valuable ally in the future. I would be foolish to throw away a chance to meet someone who could be so valuable to my career.
I see no point in false modesty, I find the core materials to be somewhat beneath my abilities. Fortunately, Jaroo has supplemented my studies with a number of more advanced tomes and parchments.
He appreciates my potential, though he constantly harps on me about the dangers of delving too deeply into the arcane. Perhaps he fears I will be devoured by my hunger for knowledge.
Still, I suppose it would be wise to heed his cautions. Perhaps I will meet with Lady Aribeth later this evening instead of studying all night, as is my usual practice.
An interesting topic, one I have studied in great detail. From a safe distance, of course.
Can you comprehend the fearsome power and terrible resolve of one who could have unleashed the Wailing Death on our city? It boggles the mind, doesn't it?
Of course. Khelben Arunsun, a mage of inestimable power, has devised a cure that can be extracted from components gathered from creatures both rare and magical.
I am no expert, but the evidence as I see it offers only one logical explanation: the source of this pestilence is magical rather than natural.
Protect the Waterdhavian creatures!
Are you threatening me? I should report you and have you expelled from the Academy! But I have not the time; I must get back to my study of these ancient tomes. Leave me be.
The evidence is obvious, is it not? Neverwinter is the only city afflicted by the Wailing Death, and the disease resists all attempts by the clergy to find a cure.
I do not know who would do such a thing, but it would require a wizard of great power. A lich, perhaps. Or possibly even the Arcane Brotherhood of Luskan. But these are just guesses.
The rumors also say the creatures have been brought here to the Academy. No doubt that is why Lady Aribeth now graces us with her presence. Perhaps I will find an opportunity to meet her later.
Sorry, I didn't mean to interrupt.
Me sorry. Me not mean to interrupt.
I think I'll be going now.
What's your problem? I'm just trying to be friendly.
Me go now.
Why you so mad? Me just want be talk at you.
What do you have against Lady Aribeth?
How's your training going?
I want to ask you a few questions.
Why you not like Aribeth?
How you training going?
Me want ask you some questions.
What can you tell me about the plague?
What can you tell me about those rumors of a cure for the plague?
How do you like training here at the Academy?
What you know 'bout plague?

You like training at Academy?
I won't take much of your time. I promise.
Me speak at you quick. Me promise me not use much time.
You better answer my questions if you know what's good for you!
You answer me question or you be sorry!
Can you blame people for losing faith? After all, you can't help them.
Why you mad people lose faith? You not help them anyway.
I have no time to talk with you - I am very busy preparing the sacred devotional rituals. You are a <class>, I am sure you understand.
I have no time to talk. The Academy might go easy on a <class> like you, but we who serve the divine will have many tasks and duties we must perform.
I see you have returned. Is there something else you need?
Forgive me. I did not mean to be so harsh, but I am very busy. Elynwyd, my mentor in the divine arts, has ordered me to make preparations for us to honor Lady Aribeth's arrival.
I suppose I can spare a few minutes for you. My heart is not in the preparations to honor Lady Aribeth, anyway. A waste of time, in my opinion.
Then I shall return to the duties Elynwyd has assigned me. May the blessings of Tyr be upon you.
It is part of my duties to provide guidance and advice to my fellow students here at the Academy. Ask your questions.
Many regard Aribeth de Tylmarande as a champion of Tyr and a defender of our faith, but where does she seek salvation during these difficult times? In the works of the wizard Khelben Arunsun!
Knowing this, how can I join the others who praise and fawn over her? But Aribeth has authority in this matter, and I am only a lowly acolyte. So I perform my duties as ordered.
The path of worship is demanding. Only those who are strong in their faith have the strength to persevere and complete their training.
But my faith is strong and true. I live to serve the divine will, and I will not abandon my beliefs as others - like Lady Aribeth - seem to have done.
I have heard many rumors of the plague. Some say it is unnatural, that it was brought about through fell magic by enemies of Neverwinter. But I do not believe this.
The citizens have lost their faith. Even the priests and clerics of the city have faltered. That is why the plague resists our attempts to cure it with prayer and holy magic.
Everyone speaks of the cure discovered by the wizard Khelben Arunsun, but I refuse to abandon my faith and place my hope in works of sorcery.
I believe the Wailing Death is a divine trial, a test of our faith and resolve. Unfortunately, we seem to be failing this test.
We are under attack!
I dare not shed blood in this holy place, so I will ignore your threats. Otherwise I would show you the power of the God I serve! Begone, infidel!
As I said, this is a trial of our faith. People who once worshipped with us now turn against the clergy because we cannot help them. But the fault is theirs, not ours. They are weak in their beliefs.
Ultimately this trial - as all trials of faith - shall pass. Those who hold true to the spiritually divine will survive the plague. The hypocrites will be exposed and shall perish.

For the sake of Neverwinter, I hope her folly brings us a cure for the Wailing Death. But in my heart I know the will of the divine alone can save us. Aribeth's misguided efforts will only prolong our suffering.
