Since before the founding of the city of Waterdeep, an infamous dungeon known as Undermountain has existed beneath it. While full of many dangers, Undermountain has never threatened the city... until now.

For reasons unknown, Waterdeep is now suddenly under siege from forces originating within Undermountain. A call has gone out for heroes to deal with this mysterious threat, and it is to this call that you have responded.

Upon your arrival in Waterdeep late in the night, you were ushered to the Yawning Portal, an inn which holds access to Undermountain itself. Here you and other adventurers are to meet with the proprietor, Durnan, to organize yourselves for what is to come.

You've been approached Nathyrra, a drow who claims to be an agent for a mysterious group of rebels opposing the dark elves attacking Waterdeep. According to Nathyrra, the armies invading Waterdeep are being controlled by a powerful drow House Mother known only as the Matron. If Nathyrra is telling the truth, you may have a new ally in your quest to save Waterdeep. But if she's lying, trusting her could be deadly...

Descent into Undermountain
The Yawning Portal has come under attack, the drow striking from Undermountain even as Durnan was in the middle of preparing an expedition to go in and explore the dungeon's depths.

The raids on Waterdeep are getting worse; even Durnan's inn has been attacked, as you know first hand. The drow sent to steal your equipment was likely only the first strike against you. The next time the results could be far more lethal.

Your only hope of stopping the attacks - both on Waterdeep and on you - is to go into Undermountain and discover why Halaster's magic no longer keeps those inside the dungeon from escaping to the surface.

Durnan feels the mad mage himself is to blame, but it is possible something may have happened to Halaster. And if so, what new enemy is behind these attacks? The answers await you below... if you survive.

You've learned that Halaster has disappeared, leaving Undermountain in chaos. With the mage gone, the protections keeping the creatures from leaving his dungeon have also vanished.

Durnan would be interested in what you have learned, though no doubt he will want you to try and discover where Halaster has gone, and why he left.

Durnan was interested in the news of Halaster's disappearance, and he's urged you to try and find out more. Has something happened to Halaster, or is his disappearance part of some grand, sinister scheme?

Halaster has been captured by the drow. With the mad mage out of the picture, the dark elves are moving freely through Undermountain, allowing them to strike at Waterdeep.

Durnan should be given this information as soon as possible, though he will likely want you to investigate these drow further.

To say Durnan was troubled by the news that Halaster has been captured by the drow would be an understatement. The innkeeper has asked you to try and discover more about this new enemy, including who is leading them and how they managed to imprison an archmage of Halaster's stature.

The answers you seek can only be found in the depths of Undermountain itself.

The leader of the drow invaders is a matron mother known only as 'The Valsharess'. Though you still know little about her, you should at least advise Durnan of the name of the one who is behind the attacks on Waterdeep.

As expected, Durnan has asked you to try and discover more about the Valsharess.. including a way to stop her and her followers from destroying Waterdeep. According to Durnan, the key to stopping them is finding and releasing Halaster. Once the mad mage is in control of undermountain again, the attacks should come to an end.

You've rescued Halaster from the clutches of the drow, and as a reward the wizard cast you down into the Underdark to exact vengeance on the Valsharess for imprisoning him. He also cast a geas on you to ensure your loyalty. Unless you find some other way to break the archmage's spell, the only way to free yourself from his service is to find the Valsharess and kill her.

On the bright side, Halaster did promise to end the attacks on Waterdeep.

It is said that both you and Mephistopheles returned to the Nine Hells in the end, the archdevil ruling alongside you for a thousand years. He coached you on the treacherous ways of the Baatezu and kept you from harm, his loyalty to you secured by the power of his True Name. Together you waged many wars of conquest and for a time your influence spread throughout the Outer Planes. Legend claims that Mephistopheles would one day attempt to trick you as he did the Valsharess, but that in the end you humiliated him with defeat once more. This, however, is another story.

Though it meant a return to the Outer Planes, it is said that the great archdevil Mephistopheles was bound to your service by your use of his True Name. News from the depths of the Nine Hells is ever unreliable, but some claim that he served you faithfully, bowing and scraping before you even as he longed for your mortal life to expire. Some tales relate that Mephistopheles would attempt to trick you as he did the Valsharess, but that in the end you humiliated him with defeat once more. That, however, is another story.

It is said that the archdevil Mephistopheles abandoned his war of conquest, his desire to subjugate the mortal realms foiled by his defeat at your hands. He fled the world of Toril, never to return. Such tales rarely end so easily, however, and future stories claimed that Mephistopheles spent much of his future consumed with the desire for revenge upon the one who humbled him. Whether his plots proved successful, however, or whether you vanquished him again as you had the first time is another tale.

[MEPHISTOPHELES - FATE 2] Becomes kindhearted.

Commanded by his True Name, Mephistopheles had no choice but to obey. Every goodly act festered like a wound upon his heart, driving him to madness. Yet every good act begat another and another and threefold more until all that was devilish within him was consumed...

It is said that the great archdevil Mephistopheles collapsed into dust and existed no more. The world shuddered with his passing and all grew still for a time, but bringing an end to such beings is rarely so simple. Some tales claimed that Mephistopheles could never be completely destroyed on the Material Plane. They say his will lived on, and out of a desire for vengeance his body was eventually reformed on the Outer Planes. A day of reckoning was sure to follow someday... though that is another tale.

From the ashes of the devil's gambit, Waterdeep rose again, rebuilt and renewed with all the fervor of a vast and bustling city, its place as the jewel of Faerun reclaimed. Reunited with his family, Durnan restored the Yawning Portal to its former glory. He hung a portrait of you upon the mantelpiece and told your tale to all who sought the fire's warmth...

With your help, the havoc unleashed by the devil's gambit allowed an opportunity for you to gain power. Waterdeep was rebuilt under Durnan's guidance but other realms did not fare as well as your lust for conquest turned more and more of those cities under your thumb into a true, living hell. The legends claim that one day your power would be challenged and your terrors would become but a memory... but not now. And so you sat upon your darkened throne, pondering all the evils you had wrought...

Daelan Red Tiger returned to his homelands in the frozen north and accepted a position among the Elders of his Uthgardt tribe, finally finding the sense of acceptance and belonging he had sought for so many years. The tales say that the great Daelan lived to a ripe old age, fathering many children. He guarded the frozen northlands with a legendary sense of justice, combating many evils and seeing the Uthgardt through the most difficult times in their history. When the great barbarian breathed his last, his spirit was said to have risen and taken its place amongst the stars over Faerun, an inspiration for future outcasts to come.

After his experience in Undermountain, Tomi Undergallows left the Yawning Portal under suspicious circumstances and rumors of missing cutlery. Where he went from there is unknown, but tall tales of his exploits soon began to emerge. Tomi was said to be involved in a scheme to steal Elminster's pipe and, strangely, he was even reported to have ruled the pirate city of Luskan for a time. The truth of these tales is questionable at best and only one story is said to have any real merit: it is claimed that, shortly after leaving Waterdeep, Tomi met his end at the hand of a ragged, giggling maniac known only as "Sammy..."

As for Linu La'neral, she finally returned to her home city of Evereska. The temple there, dedicated to Sehanine Moonbow, at long last forgave her for the accidents of her past and granted her the title of High Priestess. It took only a month for Linu to reduce the temple to ruins (purely an accident, of course) and she returned to Waterdeep once more. There she was said to have been a force of good in troubled times, guiding its citizens with a sense of justice and diplomacy that, as once noted by the Sage Elminster, "held all the grace that her feet did not."

Sharwyn wrote a soulful ballad based on her experiences in Undermountain that somehow found its way to Cormyr and the ears of its Infant-King, Azoun V. Greatly enthralled, the young king insisted that she be offered a court position as Bard Laureate of the capital, Suzail. She accepted eagerly, her songs soon becoming an inspiration to the kingdom. Later stories emerged, suggesting that she fell in love with a man as gentle of heart as he was hideous in appearance. Abandoning her wealth and position, she left the security of the King's service to live in blissful poverty with her one true love. She was the beauty to his beast and their love would spawn a legend of its own... and Sharwyn, at last, would find the true happiness she so desperately sought.

Deep in the Underdark, the wake of your passing is still felt. The Seer survived Mephistopheles' pillage of the region and became renowned as a leader of her people. Her followers still scour the depths for drow seeking to escape the despair and treachery of their life, bringing those they find to a new existence on the surface. The task is not an easy one, however, as the drow matrons constantly send assassins into the fold. But the Seer still survives and still names you in her prayers. Amongst her and her followers, you are remembered as a friend to all those who sought solace from the shadows...

Deep in the Underdark, the wake of your passing is still felt. The Seer survived Mephistopheles' pillage of the region and her followers still search for those drow looking to escape the despair and treachery of their life, bringing those they find to a new existence on the surface. Thanks to the power of the Shattered Mirror that you left with her, her job is much easier than it once was. The church of Eilistraee grow steadily in strength and your name is praised as a true friend of those who seek refuge from the shadows...

Deep in the Underdark, memories of your betrayal persisted for many years. The followers of Eilistraee were all dead by your treachery, however, and none were left to curse your name. Among the drow houses, you are honored as a devious outsider who showed no mercy for the weak...

With the help of the Shattered Mirror, the illithid of Zorvak'Mur quickly came to dominate their region of the Underdark, driving back the drow and other lesser races. Under the guidance of the Overmind, many of them infiltrated secret societies of the surface world, spreading their influence far and wide even there...

With the death of their Overmind, the illithid of Zorvak'Mur easily fell prey to the treachery of their so-called allies. The alliance between the illithid and the drow died with the Valsharess. It was not long before all at the outpost were enslaved to rival drow houses, their psionic powers tightly controlled, while the rest of their race returned to their previous doctrine of war against lesser enemies.

Despite the death of the Valsharess, the alliance she forged with the illithid persisted, becoming one of the defining features of her legacy. Under the protection of the drow and the guidance of the Overmind, the illithid flourished, many of them infiltrating the secret societies of the surface world...

Enraged by the slaughter of his priesthood, the dracolich Vix'thra unleashed his wrath upon the village of Drearing's Deep. There were no survivors and the occasional mushroom is all that now lives amidst the blasted rubble. Ghosts are still said to haunt the place, however, and one of them, a lowly rock gnome, is said to cry your name out in rage and despair...

Freed from both the priesthood's brutal rule and the wrath of the dracolich, Vix'thra, the community of Drearing's Deep struggled mightily to provide a refuge amidst the many evil races of the Underdark. Countless village leaders died in battle, though their spirit was never broken. Rumors spoke of an addled but kind-hearted rock-gnome who served as the community's true leader, masterminding its strategies from behind the scenes. Whatever the case, the freemen of Drearing's Deep survived battle after battle until, in time, the city became a veritable fortress, a bastion of hope for those yet enslaved and a proud beacon of freedom for those who had recently escaped...

As for Cania, little changed. Devils continued to mine their ice for the walls of Mephistar, the Spirits of the Dead continued to arrive and slowly join the ranks of the Lost, and the vast glacial wastes continued to hold the Knowers and their secrets close, buried deep beneath the glacial ice...

As for Cania, it is said to have achieved new greatness under your rulership, at least for a time. The City of Lost Souls, long neglected by Mephistopheles, grew into a thriving metropolis rivaling that of Sigil itself. Vast armies of the fiendish dead marched under your command, their fearsome weapons forged from the glacial ice. Few would ever uncover the secret to your power, however, and any who did were quickly silenced. For to rule the Hells, you had long since realized that you must keep your enemies close... and the Knowers even closer.

As for Cania, the disappearance of Mephistopheles left a power vacuum among the upper echelons of the Baatezu. Soon all the Hells of Baator descended into a vicious bloodbath as devil fought against devil, all of them eager for the throne. Wise as they may be, the Knowers were powerless against the onslaught and soon passed away amidst the slaughter's frenzy. Only the dread Asmodeus remained uninvolved, nursing his ancient wounds, content to let his lessers fight amongst themselves...

As for Cania, Mephistopheles surrendered it to the Knowers as you had commanded him. When the last of the devils had retreated through the Gatehouse, it is said that Cania finally slipped its moorings and became a separate plane once more, no longer the frozen Hell of Baator. Some stories claimed that other devils waged a long war in the years to come to retrieve it, but whether or not it was re-conquered is unknown. The Knowers held your name in reverence for ages to come, a mystery that scholars of the planes found intriguing as so little else was known of you...

[KNOWERS - FATE 3] Meph returns or devils are not reined in.

Angered by the role played by the Knowers in their master's downfall, lynch mobs of vengeful devils began to scour the Wastes of Cania, finally hunting the Knowers to extinction. The Knower of Places was the last to be found but even she could not hide away from the world forever...

[KNOWERS - FATE 2] Freed from persecution.

Freed from persecution, the handful of surviving Knowers emerged from hiding and reclaimed their homeland, rebuilding it as a hidden plane of advanced learning and esoteric knowledge much sought after but rarely found...

[KNOWERS - FATE 1] Names & Places involved in Sleeping Man love triangle.

With the Knower of Names' newfound freedom, the long-standing tension that existed between her and her sister, the Knower of Places, soon dissolved. They resolved their differences regarding the Sleeping Man and it was rare to see one without the other ever since...

The years passed and the Sleeping Man slept much as he had for so many years before. Sometimes he dreamed of his long journey and sometimes he dreamed of yours. But most of all he dreamed of his one true love, her face and name forever hidden from him. The years passed and the Sleeping Man slept, his faith and hope eternal...

At long last, the Sleeping Man woke in the embrace of the woman he believed to be his one true love, his long dark night having finally reached its dawn. Together, they traveled the planes, their lives an endless honeymoon, free of worry or concern. Legends say they're out there still, charting a course between the distant stars...

The Sleeping Man waited patiently for your return and when you did, he loved you fully, with all of his heart. As the years passed you came to love him in return until your souls were so entwined that it was no longer possible to tell where one ended and the next began. In this way, you came to be immortal, as was he...

Robbed of the woman he believed to be his one true love, the Sleeping Man fell into a deep despair. All hope left him and slowly, over the course of generations, he was claimed by the ice of Cania, his spirit joining with those of the Lost...

The ghost of Aribeth de Tylmarande wandered the mortal realm for many years, chaos and treachery following in her wake. She eventually turned her attention to the city of Neverwinter that she had once called home and there she haunted it with every fiber of her being. Calamity after calamity fell upon the city. Aribeth's name becoming a thing whispered only in fear and despair, until finally a hero came to the beleaguered city to stand against the ghost's tyranny and was victorious. That, however, is another tale...

The ghost of Aribeth de Tylmarande reveled with you amidst the heady spoils of war. She never grew old. She never lost her beauty nor did her passion for you fade. You loved each other until you were old and gray and triumphant. As you died, she leaned close, nibbling on your ear. "I shall see you in the Hells," she whispered. She lingered on this plane for a time after your death until finally departing forever. The legends say that the two of you did meet once again in the Hells, as promised, continuing a reign of terror amongst the devils and planars...

Despite her betrayal in the final hour, you spared the ghost of Aribeth de Tylmarande a second and final death. She made no apologies but bowed low, acknowledging your prowess, before turning her back on you and departing through the city's shattered streets. You haven't seen her since but you can feel the malevolence of her spirit out there, somewhere, cruel and triumphant...

Dark-hearted and treacherous to the end, the ghost of Aribeth de Tylmarande was destroyed in the battle against Mephistopheles. As she died her second death, you couldn't help but feel a certain pride on her behalf. Even though she betrayed you, she remained true to the evil within herself...

The ghost of Aribeth de Tylmarande wandered the mortal realm for many years, eventually returning to the city of Neverwinter that was once her home. There she helped the sick, the lame, the poor until little by little, she felt the burden of her penance lifted. Some say that the Wounded God, Tyr, finally appeared to her then to welcome her at long last to the plane of Lunia. Tears filling her eyes, the ghost of Aribeth finally left this world forever. Only then did she find rest, a gentle spirit at last forgiven...

The ghost of Aribeth de Tylmarande never grew old. She never lost her beauty nor did her passion fade. You loved each other until you yourself became old and gray, and in your dying breath you promised that you would meet her on the other side. Aribeth wept after your passing and then herself faded from this world. Legend claims that she met you once more in the next life as promised, and that your love continues on... as do your adventures...

Overwhelmed with the guilt of having betrayed you in the final hour, Aribeth de Tylmarande begged for your forgiveness. Knowing that the true guilt lay with Mephistopheles, you sheathed your wrath and granted her your clemency. After that night, she remained loyal to you forevermore...

Destroyed in battle, the treacherous spirit of Aribeth de Tylmarande at last found rest. She was both fierce and fragile all at once, even to the end. As she died her second death, you could not help but feel that there was an intrinsic goodness to her, deep and at the root...

Nathyrra found a new life on Toril's surface, dwelling amongst the followers of the Seer. Using her training as a Red Sister, she served the Church by returning frequently to the Underdark, infiltrating her own kind to hold secret services within their midst and thereby spread the Seer's teachings. As a result of her bravery, many drow abandoned their foul worship of Llolth, the spider-god, in favor of Eilistraee's more enlightened teachings and one by one, she helped them make the long journey out of the enclosing darkness and into the surface light.

Nathyrra finally reached the surface she had dreamed of for so long, leaving behind the demons of her past. She returned to the Underdark many times, however, using her training as a Red Sister to infiltrate her kind and spread the Seer's teachings. As a result of her bravery, many drow abandoned their foul worship of Llolth, the spider-god, in favor of Eilistraee's more enlightened teachings. But after every journey into the darkness, she came back to you, the one she loved above all else, and together you learned to live under an open sky...

Ashamed by her betrayal of you, Nathyrra abandoned your company in the night, despite your efforts to forgive her. She returned to the Underdark and there rejoined with the followers of Eilistraee. Using her training as a Red Sister, she served the Church by infiltrating her own kind and holding secret services within their midst, spreading the Seer's teachings. Through her actions many drow were converted to the worship of Eilistraee but, in the quiet darkness of her heart she was never able to forgive herself for betraying you. She remained haunted by the memory and driven by it to the end of her days...

Nathyrra was killed in the final battle with Mephistopheles, a victim of her own doubts and failings. Unable to ever truly forgive herself for the crimes of her past, the darkness consumed her in the end...

The bards sing of Valen adventuring with you for a time, though the two of you eventually parted ways. The tales of his exploits throughout Faerun are many, but always the tiefling remained alone and apart from those he protected. Some claim that he found his way back to Sigil where he became an important figure within the city's powerful factions, unifying some and destroying others. Valen always remembered you as a friend and companion, however, someone with whom he had made a personal connection. He returned to you on numerous occasions, accompanying you in your exploits when he was not already embroiled in his own...

Valen escaped the loneliness of his blood at last, finding in you that other part of his soul that he had always missed. Though the two of you were not always together, you were also never truly apart, and more often than not you were inseperable during the greatest of your adventures. Even when the two of you returned to the planes, he claimed he no longer felt the call of the Blood War within his veins. His heart, he told you, was full enough with you alone...

It is said that Valen explored many places in Faerun after parting ways with you. In many ways, after betraying you, he became little more than a lost soul, doomed to wander alone forever, desiring nothing more than to be felled in battle. In time, he left Toril behind and returned to the planes, the call of the Blood War still pounding in his veins...

A victim of his own demonic taint and his inability to escape the powerful influence of the arch-devil Mephistopheles', it came as little surprise that Valen betrayed you in the end. He died in battle as he would have wanted, but his name was soon forgotten in the wake of your greater victory...
[DEEKIN REACHES END BATTLE - FATE 4] He lives out the remainder of his life.

Deekin would go on to become a legendary bard and adventurer in his own right, occasionally joining you in your exploits and often getting caught up in his own. He lived a good life in Waterdeep with many friends, becoming ever more famous and gaining the sense of confidence he had always lacked. He eventually returned as a celebrated hero to his former tribe in the Nether Mountains, however, becoming their first true diplomat and greatest chieftain. He led his tribe out of hiding and negotiated the founding of a permanent mixed-race settlement with a human farming community grateful for the protection they could offer. This unique community of kobolds became a valued bridge between the various groups of beasts and men who once had once known each other only in battle but now sought peace. Deekin's eventual passing was mourned by many... though you can be sure his legacy will live on in a new generation of Scalesingers eager to find their own adventures just as their father did before them...

Having fallen victim to Mephistopheles' manipulation, Deekin berated himself for months after his attempt to betray you. The guilt gave birth to an inner resolve, however; a commitment to be true to himself and beholding to the powers of the world no more. Armed by this decision, he went on to a rather successful adventuring career, eventually returned as a celebrated hero to his former tribe in the Nether Mountains. He became their first true diplomat and greatest chieftain, leading them out of the caverns and founding a permanent mixed-race settlement with a human farming community grateful for the protection they could offer. This unique kobold community became a valued bridge between the various groups of beasts and men who once had once known each other only in battle but now sought peace.

Turned against you at the end by Mephistopheles, Deekin died an ignoble death, never having the chance to taste the true freedom he had always craved. In betraying you, he also ultimately betrayed himself, choosing instead to serve the will of others rather than his own...

You became a terror on the face of Toril, legends claiming that your armies spread the darkness that was within your heart over the lands of Faerun. You were yet another challenge for the heroes of the land to face, and it is said that upon your inevitable defeat by the forces of good you swore revenge. In tales told by drunken bards, your spirit festers in a dungeon far beneath a plain that remembers your ancient battles only by the old bones still bleaching in the sun. One day your ambition will demand your return... or so the bards will claim.

Saved from the destruction that would have been visited upon them by Mephistopheles, the citizens of Toril joined together in showering you with their gratitude. A holiday was named in your honor, and in the days to come you would rise in power, becoming confidante to the lords of nations who sought counsel from the wisest of champions. Legends conflict in their claims of where you went after this, some saying you disappeared mysteriously and some saying you rose to become a benevolent ruler... the only surety is that your name is uttered alongside the greatest heroes the Realms has ever known.

Word of your hell-borne alliance with Mephistopheles spread far and wide throughout the planes. Armies trembled before the two of you, lords and ladies pandered to your every whim, and evil permeated the ground upon which you trod. Nothing could stop you and nothing ever did...

When all was said and done and an end put to the fiendish plans of Mephistopheles, monuments to your victory were erected throughout the world of Toril. Over time, tales of your heroism grew into legends, then into myths. It is said you walked the planes and some say you walk them still, sowing the seeds of goodness and hope wherever you go...

News of your escape from the Hells and triumph over Mephistopheles spread far and wide throughout the realms. Armies trembled before you, lords and ladies pandered to your every whim, and evil permeated the ground upon which you trod. In time, some began to wonder if life under Mephistopheles might have been kinder. Old, now, and wise, you smile to yourself... Yes, they were probably right...

With Mephistopheles bound to your service, you quickly grew in power and status. Bards penned songs of the Devil Tamer and, through your adventures, you came to live a long life of wealth and privelege. Some loved you, some feared you but all gave you their respect. You were the Devil Tamer, the Hero of Waterdeep, a legend in your own time...

Yet not all sat so well with you for, when you commanded Mephistopheles, you had placed your trust in a devil's word. You used no True Name to bind him, nor did you extinguish the fire that was his life. To the end of your days, you possessed a certainty that somewhere in the vastness of the planes, the archdevil was licking his wounds and waiting for you, plotting his revenge. You watch and wait for that day to come, and when it does you know that you will have to fight him to the last breath.
As promised, however, you built an inn of your own in Waterdeep and people came from miles around to torment the fallen devil that was its chambermaid...
END NARRATION. BASED ON VARIABLES SET THROUGHOUT THE GAME, THE PLAYER IS PRESENTED WITH THE AFTERMATH OF THEIR ACTIONS IN THE WORLD.
The end.

Like the other fiends inhabiting the town, this devil has the hunched appearance of a manual laborer. It probably works in the ice quarry with its fellow Baatezu.
The quarry worker looks at you in surprise, then peers over its shoulder to see if you were talking to anyone else. "Who, me?" it asks. "How come?"
"Then pike off, berk. I've got work to do."
"You want a fight? Well you've got one, then!"
"Well... That's actually not a bad reason. To be honest, I kind of like it... Now put 'em up, <mister/missus>!"
"Hmph. I'll show you evil, berk!"
"Demons? In Cania? Where!? Let me at them! I'll tear their hearts out! This Blood War ain't over yet!"
"Yeah, so? Are you going to make something of it?"
"Hmph! I'm not demon or devil. I'm a slaad! But don't you worry, I'll teach you the difference... I'm going to give you a lesson you'll never forget..."
"Hmph. The Hellbreath Tavern's on the south side of town. Should be enough to warm up by."
"Do I look like the barkeep, berk?"
"Gru'ul, the quarry boss, he does some trading on the side. Gotta catch him in a good mood, though..."
"The quarry's just east of town, through the Quarry Office. All the Grinders are down there."
"You won't find it here, berk. Head down the stairs to the Quarry proper and ask around down there."
"The one Lazy's stuck in? Just look for the one with the imp in the gears."
"Huh? Maybe ask the gith sensei. She knows about smart stuff like that."
The creature sighs impatiently. "She's with the githzerai Pilgrims. They come here every now and then to pay their respects at the temple and drown their sorrows at the tavern, all right?"
"Outa my way. Gru'ul gave me a holiday."
"Gotta get back to work. Gru'ul's orders..." the creature mentions by way of apology.
"Pike off," the creature mutters, shuffling off into the cold wind.
"Harrumph. The Sleeping Man, is it?" The creature spits a foul-smelling substance to the ground. "May he rot and freeze and rot again! The Hells have no room for bastards like him from Elysium."

The pale white flesh of this muscular creature is scarred from countless beatings. A scorched branding mark identifies it as a prisoner of the Blood War. It seems skittish and nervous as you approach.

Doing his best to avoid eye contact, the quarry boss tries to straighten a stack of papers on his desk. His claws get in the way, however, scattering them all over again.
"Why are you always so damn polite? Honestly, that bile you're spewing gets right under my skin and just eats away. Graugh! See that? Just the thought of it is making me twitch!"

"Hey now, True Names are dangerous things. Wars have been fought over less than that, empires have fallen. I don't have what you're looking for and, even if I did, I wouldn't give it to you, so pike off..."
"Clueless berks... Welcome to the Outer Planes, you basket-weaving nitwit! The Nine Hells of Baator, to be exact!"
"This here is the City of Lost Souls, a remote outpost in the wastes of Cania, the Eighth Hell of Baator. Look up and you'll see Maladomini, the Seventh. Dig down and you'll find the Ninth, Nessus."

"How many questions do you intend to ask, you annoying pea-brained gnat!? Some of the Hells are hot, some aren't, all right? Phlegethos, the Fourth Hell, has rivers of liquid fire! What does it matter?"
"The Big M? Tall, dark, and evil? You're lucky if you'll ever be half as bad as he is, you snot-nosed spawn of a rakshasan litter! He's the one who named me Quarry Boss, I'll have you know..."
"Get on with it, then, you smelly tongue-wagger. All this talking is making my scales itch!"
"Hrmph! What does any devil want? To slay a demon in the Blood War, to sow the seeds of evil and grow in power, to defeat Asmodeus and become Lord of the Ninth! All things come down to this!"
"Ha! Do we go for tea and play a little chess while warming our feet by his fires? Gnat-brained flat-head! The Big M has no time for the likes of me! Not that I don't have my ambitions, mind you..."

"But yes, now that you mention it, there were some nasty rumors about some drow she-wench in some distant world who discovered the Big M's True Name. It seemed too far-fetched to be true but who knows..."

"I have decided that I am not yet done with Neverwinter. Don't you think the temple there could use a malevolent spirit? Or if holy ground proves troublesome, what of the castle there?"

"It has been on my mind for some time. I dare say, it sounds like a Hell of a good time, wouldn't you agree...?"

"We are in search of the Reaper's True Name, are we not? Should we succeed, suddenly all things become possible..."
"To disturb its graveyards, despoil its grounds, and drive its citizens before me like rats. When I am done, not a single living soul will dare call that city home!"

"But I am a paladin again, something I could not have achieved without you! ...Yet this is your command and I must obey... Damn you, <FirstName>, let there be nothing more you would ask of me!"

The origin of this cloak dates back to the days when King Richard Garrison held power in Cania. It was crafted for him by his servant, a demented and twisted man named Pony Tall.

Pony was not a gifted being, but he managed to sew the cloak in a matter of just a few days. Barely resembling a cloak, Pony Tall had done the best he could and so wrapped the tattered garment up and made way to his master.

After giving the cloak to the King, Pony was slaughtered for his foul gift, his blood staining and possibly corrupting the garment.

Before tossing the cloak out along with Pony's body, King Richard put it on to mock his dead, incompetant servant. Upon doing so, he felt better - in all ways - and the cold night air ceased.

A Howl in the Night

You have stumbled upon a pack of winter wolves deep in the wastes of Cania. They seem skittish and frightened but not overtly hostile. They must have a den somewhere nearby and an alpha wolf who leads them.

The leader of a pack of winter wolves has warned you of a clan of frost giants who live nearby, deep in Cania's frozen wastes. Some of the wolf pups have been stolen and the pack would no doubt be happy to see their young safely returned.
You have freed a group of wolf pups being held captive by a nearby giant clan. The pups yipped excitedly as they raced off for the safety of their den. The pack will be relieved by their safe return.
A group of wolf pups lie slaughtered outside a giant fortress, their blood pooling in the trodden snow. You wondered if their pack will survive this endless winter without them.

You have killed the leader of a wolf pack deep in the frozen wastes of Cania. Though he was no match for you in the end, he fought with the fury of a cornered animal. Without his strength and guidance, you doubt the remainder of the pack will survive the endless winter.
A Lost Leader

In speaking with the Spirits of the Dead who cluster around the Gates of Cania, you have learned that they had a leader who had stood up to Mephistopheles when he first announced that he would be devouring their souls to fuel his undead army on the Prime Material plane. He must have done something dire to her, however, for after the confrontation, she fled to a cave in the center of the city where she now refuses to speak with anyone. The Spirits say she's becoming one of the Lost, those who have given up hope and are slowly merging with the icy essence of Cania.

You have found the cave in which the so-called Lost Leader of the Spirits of the Dead has sequestered herself. The cave rests atop a ridge in the city's heart and though she has sealed the entrance with some form of spell, you were able to hear her sobs echoing from deep within. A strange dog-like creature paced back and forth, whining outside the cave's entrance.

You were able to guide the strange dog-like creature you found outside the Lost Leader's cave to where it needed to be. Once led to the right location, it shot a beam of energy into the city's icy walls, carving the Spirit Leader's name into the ice so she could finally become one of the lost. Leaning closer, you were able to read the newly carved name: "Aribeth de Tylmarande." Curious, you wonder if the magical barrier she had placed at the cave entrance has faded with her passing.

There, in an ice-sheathed cavern at the heart of the City of Lost Souls, you beheld Aribeth de Tylmarande, the Lost Leader of the Spirits of the Dead. A thick layer of frost clings to her once-lithe frame, her ghostly shape at last made solid by the ice of Cania. Half-burned logs rest in a blackened pit before her, their flames long since quenched by the cavern's icy chill.

In an effort to thaw the frozen statue of Aribeth de Tylmarande, the Lost Leader of the Spirits of the Dead, you have expended a single precious velox berry to create a fire. Unfortunately, the paltry flames did little to combat the cavern's icy chill and were soon extinguished.

In an effort to thaw the frozen statue of Aribeth de Tylmarande, the Lost Leader of the Spirits of the Dead, you have expended two precious velox berries to create a fire. While the flames were sufficient to warm the confined space of the cavern, they were not enough to penetrate the icy chill that still clings to Aribeth's ghostly form.

Thanks to your efforts, Aribeth de Tylmarande, the Lost Leader of the Spirits of the Dead was rescued from the bitter chill of Cania. To your surprise, she expressed her gratitude by drawing her ghostly blade and pressing you to the attack.

Lost and now found, hostile and now pacified, Aribeth de Tylmarande, the ghostly leader of the Spirits of the Dead has surrendered herself to your will. It seems she has given up on life, even the threadbare shred experienced by the Spirits of the Dead. For your efforts to rescue her from the icy grasp of Cania to go unwasted, you will have to speak with her and convince her that she has something worth living for.

You have rescued Aribeth de Tylmarande, the ghostly leader of the Spirits of the Dead, from the icy grip of Cania. Thanks to your efforts and persistence, she has dedicated what remains of this threadbare afterlife to the cause of good. With that, you have restored her to her former paladinhood and she has offered to aid you in your quest through hell.

You have rescued Aribeth de Tylmarande, the ghostly leader of the Spirits of the Dead, from the icy grip of Cania. Thanks to your efforts and persistence, she has dedicated what remains of this threadbare afterlife to the cause of evil. With that, you have restored her to her former status as a fearsome Blackguard and she has offered to aid you in your quest through hell.
Arden Swift

Trapped here much like you, a group of Githzerai Pilgrims have related an interesting tale regarding a certain fellow named Arden Swift who has been traveling with them for the past while. According to the prevailing gossip, Arden got into an argument with the Pilgrims' leader regarding his sacriligious plans to wake the so-called Sleeping Man who the Pilgrims are here to visit. Arden's currently drowning his sorrows in the Hellbreath Tavern in the city's southeast corner.

You have met a jester, Arden Swift, in the Hellbreath Tavern in the city's southeast corner. He seems somehow associated with the Githzerai Pilgrims currently patronizing the establishment but, given his tiefling heritage and the dirty looks they occasionally slip him over their half-empty tankards, you're unsure how.

In talking with Arden Swift, a bard traveling with the Githzerai, he has told you of his rather sacriligious plans to wake their so-called Sleeping Man using a Trumpet of Pandemonium he acquired somewhere in his travels. Due to a quick intervention on the part of the Pilgrims' Sensei, the jester's plan never came to pass but he still carries the trumpet and it might be possible to convince him to part with it.

Arden Swift, patron of the Hellbreath Tavern and itinerant jester currently taveling with the entourage of Githzerai Pilgrims, has placed his beloved Trumpet of Pandemonium as a prize for an upcoming card game. He had intended to used the trumpet to wake the so-called Sleeping Man but had been caught red-handed by the Pilgrims' Sensei before he could sound its blast. If you're interested in acquiring it for yourself, you merely have to place your ante on the table and guess the card he's holding in five questions or less. You're not entirely sure if you can trust him but it might be worth a try.

With some quick thinking and a good eye, you were able to win Arden Swift's Trumpet of Pandemonium in a game of cards. Although he cheated regularly throughout the actual game, he was good on his word and handed over the trumpet as soon as you won. You suspect he was more interested in the antes you put in, as he's probably racked up a hefty tab with the rather evil-looking bartender.

In a visit to the Hellbreath Tavern, you managed to pickpocket a trumpet from the jester Arden Swift. It looks dented and old. Though its sound quality probably leaves something to be desired, you're pretty sure it's going to be loud.

In a visit to the Hellbreath Tavern, you managed to pick a fight with the jester Arden Swift. Rummaging through his pack when it was all done, you found a strange-looking trumpet, dented and old. Though its sound quality probably leaves something to be desired, you're pretty sure it's going to be loud.
Using the Trumpet of Pandemonium you acquired from Arden Swift, you were able to do the unthinkable: wake the Sleeping Man...

Peering into an ice crystal that that thrust itself up from Cania's glacial floor, you saw a vision of Mephistopheles' progress in the Prime Material Plane. It appears that he has discovered the carnage left behind by the Seer's defeat. As he passed through the rotting carcasses, they rose in his wake, a ghostly army bound to do his bidding...

Peering into an ice crystal that that thrust itself up from Cania's glacial floor, you saw a vision of Mephistopheles' progress in the Prime Material Plane. It appears that, together with his newly created army, he is slowly winding his way to the surface, sowing destruction in his wake. Mephistopheles seems to feed off the ruin he is causing. With every moment, he grows stronger...

Peering into an ice crystal that that thrust itself up from Cania's glacial floor, you saw a vision of Mephistopheles' progress in the Prime Material Plane. It appears that he has made his way to the surface, emerging in the Yawning Portal. Many of the patrons were incinerated by his deadly gaze, though you don't yet know the fate of Durnan and his family. Even so, time grows short and the city of Waterdeep is in great peril.
Escape from the Hells

The familiar blackness of death enveloped you but the blood-red eyes of your betrayer, Mephistopheles, lingered to the end. And then you woke to find your eyes reflected in the Gatekeeper's shimmering skin. Everything seems strangely familiar...

The archdevil Mephistopheles has played you for a fool. He has commanded your mysterious ally, the Gatekeeper, to bar your return to Waterdeep on the Prime Material plane, trapping you instead in some hellish world called Cania. The Gatekeeper seems sympathetic to your plight but claims he has no choice but to obey for Mephistopheles has commanded him by his True Name. Such names seem to have a strange power in this place and it seems the only way to break Mephistopheles' prohibition will be learn the Gatekeeper's True Name for yourself.

Your search for the Gatekeeper's True Name has turned up its first clue: one of the citizens of this strange city claims that an old and venerable creature known as the Sleeping Man might have the information your looking for. He sleeps in the city's northwest quarter and apparently has done so for longer than anyone can remember. Hopefully, with his help, you'll be able to return home to Waterdeep and take your vengeance on the archdevil Mephistopheles.

The Sleeping Man was not as helpful in your quest for the Gatekeeper's True Name as you had hoped. You did learn, however, of an ancient race called the Knowers that populated Cania before it was colonized by the legions of hell. One of them, the Knower of Names, was banished by Mephistopheles to an unknown prison deep in Cania's frozen wastelands. Unable to find the Knower of Names, the Sleeping Man instead sought out her sister, the Knower of Places, with the help of a magical ring that that served as his guide through Cania's wastes. If you can repeat his feat, perhaps she will be able to help you find her sister's hidden prison. The Sleeping Man broke the ring into three parts and hid it in a guarded room below his chambers. It seems your journey will begin there.

The Sleeping Man's ring that will lead you to the Knower of Places and hopefully to the Gatekeeper's True Name is a strange artifact indeed. When you slip it onto your finger, it is as if you can see into another sort of space, another dimension. Some things are present there that are not present in the real world and some things you would expect to find have disappeared. One thing you are grateful to see, however, are a line of glowing arrows that will hopefully chart a safe course through Cania's vast wastelands. You feel the stirrings of hope in your chest for the first time since Mephistopheles banished you to this frozen place.

Tormented by her loneliness, the Knower of Places has agreed to help you on your quest for the Gatekeeper's True Name. She has woven a new magic into the Sleeping Man's ring, allowing it to guide you to her sister, the Knower of Names, just as it guided you to her. She left you with a cryptic parting message that will hopefully aid you when you reach her sister's icy prison: "You are not the first to seek the prison and not the first to find it. At 7 o'clock a hole was dug and a fearsome devil freed. If he'd have come but sixteen hours prior, he'd have uncovered what you need." Hopefully you'll be able to compel the Gatekeeper to return you to Waterdeep before Mephistopheles has destroyed your home forever.

At long last you have learned the True Name of the Gatekeeper: Hecugoth the Abandoned. You say it aloud a few times, rolling it around on your tongue. It has sad sound to it but you are eager to put it to use. It's your ticket out of here, back to Waterdeep and the Prime Material or whatever still remains of them after the chaos that Mephistopheles has sown in your absence. The Relic of the Reaper will take you back to the Gates of Cania but you pause to consider whether you have any pressing tasks you wish to accomplish on this plane before you go. Facing Mephistopheles won't be easy and you'd better have made your peace with the world.

Commanded by his True Name, the Gatekeeper has opened a Planar Gate that will lead you back home to Waterdeep. Mephistopheles won't be expecting you so you'll have to take advantage of whatever element of surprise you have. It will pay to be well-prepared before you step through that gate.

Waterdeep is in shambles and your sudden appearance has brought scant hope to Durnan and the handful of citizens and soldiers still trying to resist Mephistopheles' forces. It's clear they're fighting a war of movement, winning what battles they can and surrendering ground whenever Mephistopheles himself makes an appearance. Though you dared not say it in their presence, you doubt their ragtag resistance will survive much longer without your assistance. This time, when Durnan retreats from Mephistopheles' advance, you intend to be waiting for him.

Amidst the chaos of battle and shattered streets, Durnan and his brave but dwindling army retreated from Mephistopheles' approach. The arch-devil towers over the city's architecture, reducing it to rubble with a gaze. There, in the scattered remnants of the proudest city of the Prime Material, you prepare to make your stand against the devil's onslaught...

And with that, Mephistopheles is defeated. Dark clouds linger in the graying sky above, the sounds of battle slowly growing still in the distance. Weary yet triumphant, you stop to ponder the significance of your victory...

While exploring the Temple of the Sleeping Man in the city's northwest corner, you've managed to pick the lock on one of the doors. It leads to the Inner Sanctum where the temple's namesake is said to rest.

In the holy confines of the Temple of the Sleeping Man, you have successfully recited his Five-Fold Mysteries before the Sensei Dharvana. Your reward is a crystalline amulet that she says will help you focus your thoughts on the dreams of the Sleeping Man, provided you have any latent psionic powers. The door into the temple's Inner Sanctum is now unlocked to you.

Defiling the holy confines of the Temple of the Sleeping Man, you have assassinated its leader, the Sensei Dharvana. Looting through her bloodied corpse, you found an interesting crystalline amulet about her neck. You pocket it surreptitiously, eager to explore the remainder of the temple.

There, in the temple's Inner Sanctum, with the winged form of the Sleeping Man prostrate before you, you tried in vain to make use of the Sensei's amulet. The crystal glowed a murky green when in his presence and you could feel its growing hum but you somehow lacked the wisdom to tap into its psionic powers.

There, in the temple's Inner Sanctum, with the winged form of the Sleeping Man prostrate before you, you made use of the Sensei's amulet. The crystal glowed a murky green when in his presence and you could feel its growing hum and then, all at once, you found yourself swept up within his dreams.

There, in the temple's dim green light, the Sensei's amulet clasped about your neck, you dreamed the dreams of the Sleeping Man. Mephistopheles was there and a woman called the Knower of Names, whom he banished. And an older woman, the Knower of Places, whom the Sleeping Man had visited in search of his one true love. Throughout his quest, he was somehow guided by a ring that now lies, buried and guarded, in a chamber below him. If you hope to find the Knowers, you will need that ring upon your finger...
There, in the temple's dim green light, you have done the unthinkable and woken the Sleeping Man. Hopefully he will be able to tell you the Gatekeeper's True Name.

In waking the Sleeping Man, you unleashed the Sensei's fury. Driven mad with rage, she attacked and you had no choice but to defend yourself. Now she lies dead at the feet of the Sleeping Man who she worshiped. About her neck is a crystalline amulet. You snap it off, casually pocketing it as you have so many other treasures taken from the bodies of the dead.

The Sleeping Man knows many things but, sadly, the Gatekeeper's True Name is not one of them. Even so, he tells of a race of creatures called the Knowers who once called Cania home. One of them, the Knower of Names was banished by Mephistopheles long ago while the other, the Knower of Places, lives in hiding deep in Cania's frozen wastelands. His own quest had brought him the latter's hidden lair, long ago, a feat made possible only with the aid of an enchanted ring. The ring lies in a chamber under the temple, guarded and kept safe all these many years. He has invited you to make use of the ring, provided you can claim it, and wishes you well on your journey.

"Be careful what you say here. There is a tension in Lith My'athar between the followers of the Seer and the drow of House Maeviir."
"Be on your guard. We are venturing into the true depths of the Underdark now."
"The darkness here is often filled with unseen dangers. Watch the shadows carefully."
"The Valsharess has many allies, but at the first sign of weakness they will turn on her. This is the way of the Underdark."
"Those who live on Toril's surface fear the drow, but far worse things than my people exist down here."
"The Underdark has no seasons; no cycle of night and day. I find the constant darkness... comforting."
"In the Underdark, you are either hunter or prey. Often you become the latter when you least expect it."
"An imposing fortress, to say the least. I doubt whoever's inside will be happy to see us."
"There is something foul in this place; it smells of ancient evil."
"I see the drow are not the only ones who like to throw their slaves into the pits to do battle."
"Can you feel it? A presence, thrumming against the walls of the skull. Guard your thoughts carefully."
"The Eye Tyrant must be close... and I doubt she will be unguarded."
"The stench of smoke and ash in this place is enough to make one gag!"
"Be careful of this woman. I suspect she is more than she appears."
"No doubt many traps and monsters lay ahead... typical for any wizard's tower."
"A jester without an audience... does nothing in this town make sense?"
"The town is gone! Imagine the power necessary to make a whole town disappear!"
"There are duergar nearby. The thick stink of their sweat fills the air."
"These golems are unlike any constructs I have seen before!"
"Be careful. Wizards who seek to prolong their life often turn themselves into powerful undead."
"The chill here is enough to freeze your very soul."
"You can feel the heat of the fire, even from here. Let's move closer and warm ourselves."
"I didn't expect it to be so warm in here."
"Look there - a woman, frozen in ice. No, wait... I think she's an elf."
"A jester in the Hells? Well, I suppose if anyone needs to be amused it's the souls trapped here."
"A mimic... but it doesn't seem to be attacking. It only seems interested in devouring gems."
"I don't see a bridge. We'll have to find some other way to cross this river of fire."
"A door made of... lightning?This looks like a trap - or a test. These levers must be the key."
"The Valsharess won't stop until she has conquered every land on the face of Toril."
"The Seer believes you will save us all from the Valsharess. I pray she is right."
"The Valsharess will send her assassins after us, but I know all their tricks."
"The creatures of the Underdark can strike without warning... as can I."
"The Seer has seen the future if we fail. The Valsharess will crush all of Toril beneath her boot heel."
"We drow are unwelcome on Toril's surface. The Seer told me that even the followers of Eilistraee face persecution and prejudice."
"Blood is easily wiped from a dagger's edge, but it is not so easily washed from your hands."
"I rarely used poison on my victims; I preferred the quick cut of a blade or the blast of my magic. It seemed more clean, more pure."
"I was taught to keep my blades sharp and a spell always at the ready. Old habits die hard."
"A wise mage knows that *when* a spell is cast is almost as important as *which* spell is cast. Preparation is often the key to battle."
"As an assassin, I was trained to kill. Those skills should serve us well in this place."
"The Seer says the surface of Toril is beautiful. One day I hope to see it for myself."
"Keep a sharp eye and a sharp blade. That was my motto when I was an assassin, and it serves us well enough now."
"Eilistraee is the goddess of moonlight. One day I hope to visit the surface of Toril and see the moon for myself."
"Sarn; walk carefully. Footsteps echo here, they can alert others to our presence."
"Vith usstan! My backpack is a mess! My spell components are all mixed up. *sigh* I'll have to sort them out next time we stop."
"Hold a second. I see something I can use as a component in one of my spells... there. We can continue now."
"If you want me to cast one of my spells before a battle, just let me know."
"I was taught one must conquer to survive; kill or be killed. That lesson holds true for us now."
"*sigh* I fear there is much killing still ahead, and my heart is already stained with the blood of a thousand murders."
"I killed my first victim when I was only a girl; a male slave who displeased me. I never even knew his name. I wonder why I'm thinking of him now?"
"I always looked into the eyes of my victims as they died. Now those eyes are burned into my mind, and I can't stop thinking about them."
"An assassin needs to be invisible, even in plain sight. It was a lesson I mastered quickly... thanks in part to my magic."
"Move with care. The element of surprise can win a battle; we must be careful not to give ourselves away."
"Everywhere I look I see places we could be ambushed. We are vulnerable here, we must be prepared for anything."
"Part of me feels I belong here; a doomed soul condemned to this Hell."
"I feel pity for those trapped here. Neither alive nor dead, with no real hope of escape."
"The Valsharess is defeated, but now we have unleashed an even greater evil on Toril."
"Mephistopheles played us for fools! We have to find a way to stop him. We have to!"
"As bad as the drow may be, the surface of Toril will fare much worse under the rule of a devil!"

Magics of Golem Enhancements

When constructing golems, it is important not to forget the importance of adding enhancements through enchantments. The easiest way to accomplish this is to include spell conduits on your golem creation machine. These conduits can then be filled with the appropriate spells.

It is important to remember that the effects of spells can be altered during the creation process, often producing an unexpected result when they are passed through the spell conduit.

For example:
1. Greater Spell Mantle will improve a golem's resistance to magic.
2. Bigby's Crushing Hand increases a golem's strength.
3. Greater Sanctuary provides more protection against physical attacks.
4. Time Stop grants the golem improved regenaration.
5. Premonition results in improved damage reduction.
6. Mass Haste provides a permanent haste effect.
7. True Seeing provides a permanent True Seeing effect.
8. Chain Lightning causes a lightning bolt to be released whenever the golem is hit by an enemy.
9. Mordenkainen's Disjuntion gives the golem the ability to Dispel Magic each time it hits an opponent.

By placing these spells in the respective conduits, a golem's attributes and abilities can be customized to the creators exact specifications.

You've met Shaori, the Avariel Queen - though she is now nothing but a reclusive hermit. She mentioned something about pieces of a magical mirror and suggested you should go to the castle if you want to learn more.

You've met an odd little man who claims to be Queen Shaori's fool. He's explained to you that the town is cursed, and that the only way to remove the curse is to recover the missing pieces of a magical mirror. He believes the pieces can be found in the town's library, the temple, the wizard's tower, with the town merchant and with the Queen in her cave.

The fool has warned you that a drow named Sabal is also trying to recover the missing pieces. Once all five pieces are accounted for, you will have to return to the throne room.

All five pieces of the mirror have been recovered and the fool has returned the Avariel kingdom to its rightful place among the mountains of the Lost Peak. In exchange for your help, he's given you the mirror - a powerful but dangerous magical artifact.

The beholders who have joined the Valsharess all come from a single hive to the west of the rebel camp. It is unlikely you will be able to reason with them: if you want to weaken the Valsharess, you will have to kill the Eye Tyrant leading the colony.
With the death of the Eye Tyrant, the beholders are no longer a threat to join the army of the Valsharess.
The Seer was pleased to learn that the beholders will not be among the army of the Valsharess when the attack on Lith My'athar finally comes.

Defeating the Valsharess

Halaster has cast you down to into the Underdark and placed a geas upon you. The only way to be free of the wizard's bond is to find and destroy the Valsharess.

Fortunately, the mad mage has teleported you into the heart of a rebel drow camp, where you've met the Seer - an ally who will aid you against the Valsharess.

The Seer believes you are the only one capable of stopping the Valsharess and her massive army. You have to find some way to weaken the Valsharess and her allies, or find a way to strengthen the Seer and her band of followers.
In exchange for promising to betray the Seer and her followers, the Valsharess has removed the geas Halaster placed upon you. Now you must decide if you will go through with your treachery...

The Valsharess has approached you in a dream, and offered to remove the geas Halaster placed upon you if you betray the Seer and her followers. Though you refused her, you know that should you change your mind during the siege, the Valsharess would still welcome you...
You've betrayed the Seer and all her followers, proving her prophetic powers weren't very prophetic at all.
Mephistopheles, the devil the Valsharess managed to capture, has played you and the Valsharess against each other. This will only end when one of you is dead.

Female Slave
You've purchased a female slave from the illithid and sent her off to the fighting pits - a truly grim fate. At least you'll be able to wager on her battles... until she dies.

You've come up with a plan to gain the freedom of the female slave you purchased from the illithid. Because of the mind flayers' telepathic abilities, you can't reveal your plan to her.

You've sent her to deliver a fake message to the Seer. Since she believes she is magically bound to you, the illithid will consider her a slave in your service and allow her to leave their city. Once back at the rebel camp, you can explain the truth to her.
You've purchased a female slave from the illithid and sent her off to the fighting pits - she fought bravely but died as a gladiator.

The slave you freed from the illithid managed to find her way back to the Seer's camp. Once the threat of the Valsharess is no more, the Seer has promised to help her find her way back to the surface so she can leave the Underdark behind her forever.
The female slave from the illithid slave market has been killed.
Ferron

Ferron, the metallic leader of a group of golem rebels, has asked for your help in retrieving an artifact known as the Power Source so that he can lead the golems away from the halls of the Maker and the tyrannical rule of Aghaaz, the self-proclaimed leader of the golems on the island.

You've given Ferron the Power Source, effectively freeing the golems. As long as they keep the Power Source with them, they can freely travel to any destination they wish. In exchange for your aid, Ferron has promised that his golems will join with you when you move against the Valsharess.
Golems on an Island

The tiefling Valen told you of a nearby island that is supposed to be inhabited completely by golems. If you could find a way to control these constructs, you could use them against the Valsharess and her army.

The Boatman in the ports to the East might be able to give you more information about this.

You've learned that the Isle of the Maker was once home to a powerful duergar wizard who retired there to perfect the art of creating golems. If this wizard still lives, he might be able to help you against the Valsharess. If he's dead, you still might be able to use his creations in the coming battle.

Should you wish to investigate this island, Cavallas the Boatman can take you there.
The Seer was pleased to learn of the golem allies you acquired for her forces.
You've discovered a band of duergar on the island, but if you want to learn anything about the Maker or his golems you'll have to explore the remains of his dungeon.
You've encountered a group of sentient golems created by the Maker long ago. They've offered to help you against the Valsharess... if you first help them.
Ferron has promised to send golems to aid the Seer against the Valsharess. No doubt she will be pleased to learn of this new ally.
Aghaaz has promised to send golems to aid the Seer against the Valsharess. No doubt she will be pleased to learn of this new ally.
With the loss of the Power Source, the sentient golems have all ceased to function. Any chance you might have had of gaining their aid against the Valsharess is now lost.
Illithid Allies of the Valsharess

Nathyrra has told you of an illithid city to the west of the drow village that has allied itself with the Valsharess. If you can find some way to turn them against the Valsharess it will significantly weaken her army.

The illithid who serve the Valsharess come from a number of different colonies, and serve a number of different Overminds. However, it may be possible to persuade one of the Overminds to convince the others to withdraw their support of the Valsharess.

The small illithid colony of Zorvak'Mur is located to the west of the drow encampment. While killing the Zorvak'Mur Overmind will accomplish nothing, negotiating with it could result in all the Overminds abandoning the Valsharess.
Though you killed the Zorvak'Mur Overmind, you have failed in your mission to stop the illithid from joining the Valsharess.
The Seer was pleased to learn that the illithid have abandoned the Valshraess.
Shaori's Cave
The Fool believes one of the pieces of the shattered mirror is in the cave of Queen Shaori, located past the library in the south east of the town.

You've spoken with the former Avariel Queen. Shaori has turned her back on her people and become a hermit.

She did mention that she gave a piece of a magical mirror to a drow named Sabal, and she suggested you should investigate the castle to the north west.
You've met Shaori, the former ruler of this strange town. She's become a hermit, abandoning her throne to live alone in a cave.
Slave Revolt

You've freed a group of slaves from the pens of Zorvak'Mur. Though eager for freedom, you've convinced the slaves to wait until you reach the Elder Brain before they begin their revolt. However, you know that if their rebellion succeeds, any chance of convincing the illithid to abandon the Valsharess is likely gone.

You've freed a group of slaves from the pens of Zorvak'Mur. Under their leader, Argosus, they've launched a bid for freedom. The only downside is that you've likely destroyed any chance you had of convincing the illithid to abandon the Valsharess.

You've betrayed Argosus and his followers in order to garner the goodwill of the Zorvak'Mur Overmind. No doubt the slaves will suffer terribly for their attempted escape, but it's a price you're willing to pay.
The Beholder Caves

You have met Attiz, a Kobold slave in the Beholder caves. According to Attiz, the Beholders have stumbled upon a series of ancient tunnels beneath their own cave. Attiz claims that the Beholders have sent him down into these tunnels to explore the area. Attiz managed to retrieved an ancient stone slab before he was attacked by huge spiders, but apparently the Beholders have taken away the stone slab.
You have found the ancient slab that was supposedly retrieved by the Kobold slave Attiz. The slab might contain useful information about the ruins below.
You have disabled the ancient obelisk that nullified any kind of magic in the tunnels below the Beholder caves. It seems that the core of the obelisk can now be taken.
The Library
A guard at the library warned you of a dangerous medusa inside - a creature that was once his beautiful wife.

A guard at the library warned you of a dangerous medusa inside - a creature that was once his beautiful wife.

The guard also mentioned a way you might be able to speak with the medusa safely. There is a potion in his old bedroom in the southern side of the library that will prevent the medusa's petrifying gaze from turning you to stone.

You've spoken to the medusa inside the library, and it is obvious the transformation has left her quite insane. She seems intent on burning all the books in the building, rendering them virtually worthless.

The medusa did make mention of a shard from a broken mirror she keeps in her possession. If you can get it from her, you might be able to use it later.
The medusa is dead, slain by the Red Sisters who ambushed you earlier. Anything of value the poor librarian may have had on her has been taken by the assassins.
You've obtained the mirror shard from the medusa inside the library.
The Fool believes one of the pieces of the shattered mirror is in the library on the eastern edge of the town.
The Maker's Assistant

You've encountered a ghostly apparition of the Maker's former assistant. His spirit has been trapped for five centuries by the Maker, but he can be freed if someone will bring him a small stone known as the soul gem. In exchange, he's offered you the password to get by the Keeper, the guardian protecting the lowest levels of the dungeon.

You've convinced the Maker's assistant to give you the password to get by the Keeper so you can access the lowest levels of the dungeon. In exchange you've promised to bring him the soul gem so he can be free. Whether you actually fulfill that promise remains to be seen...
You've freed the Maker's assistant from his eternal torment and you've managed to learn the password to get by the Keeper, the guardian of the lowest levels of the dungeon.
The Merchant

You've run into a strange merchant who seems intent on getting rid of all his inventory, but only if he can do it without reaping any profits. His only remaining piece of value is a shard of a broken mirror.
He will only give it up if he is given something even less valuable in exchange.
According to the Fool, the merchant in the center of town has managed to find one of the pieces of the shattered mirror.

The merchant has given you a magical compass to lead you to his piece of the broken mirror.

When activated, the compass will flash. The closer you get to the mirror shard, the faster it will flash. Using the compass and moving slowly throughout the town you should be able to find where the shard is hidden.
You've found a shard from a broken mirror hidden in a pile of garbage, where it had been stashed by the strange merchant in the town center.
The Temple
According to the Fool, the temple on the western edge of town likely contains one of the pieces of the shattered mirror.

Upon entering the temple you were afflicted with a terrible disease. The only way to rid yourself of this plague is to get the antidote from the temple's resident priest.

He has offered you the antidote if you successfully complete a series of trials by combat. He's also promised to give you a piece of a magical mirror... should you survive.

The priest has told you that Sabal - the leader of the drow who first attacked you upon entering the town - has already completed his challenge and claimed the reward of the broken mirror shard.

However, you are still afflicted with the strange disease, and the priest is the only one who has the antidote. It seems as though you're still going to have to complete his challenge.
You have been given the cure for the strange affliction, although the mirror shard the priest once possessed is now in the hands of Sabal and her drow.
You have been given the cure for the strange affliction and managed to claim the shard of the broken mirror that was in the priest's possession.
The Wizard's Tower
The Fool believes one of the pieces of the shattered mirror is now inside the wizard's tower on the north edge of town.
Petyr, the former archmage who resided inside the tower, has informed you that he found a piece of a magical mirror and gave it to his apprentice, who now dwells within the tower.

On the last level of the tower you've come across the slain body of the wizard's apprentice. It's obvious the drow who attacked you earlier were responsible for his death, and they must have taken anything of value he may have had.
You've claimed the magical mirror shard from the wizard's apprentice.
Undead Army of the Valsharess

Nathyrra has told you that the Valsharess commands a horde of undead. She believe the source of this horde is off to the west of the rebel camp. If you could destroy these undead, it would be a significant blow to the Valsharess.

Nobody is certain where the undead horde of the Valsharess is coming from, though there are rumors of a cult of necromancers hidden in the caverns to the west of the drow rebels. If the cult could be found, the source of all these undead could also be discovered and destroyed.
The Seer was pleased to learn that the Valsharess will no longer be able to call upon the undead hosts in the coming battle.

You've discovered the source of the undead hosts: the cult of Vix'thra had imprisoned an astral deva and were using her blood to animate an army of skeletons and corpses. With the Deva freed from her bonds, the cult can no longer provide undead for the Valsharess... though Vix'thra himself could still be a threat
With Vix'thra's death the cult that was supplying the Valsharess with undead is no more. The Seer will be pleased to learn of this development.
Zorvak'Mur

On your way to the illithid city of Zorvak'Mur, you've encountered a group of duergar slavers. You've learned that the mind flayers of Zorvak'Mur allow non-illithid slavers to enter their city, but you'll need some type of mental protection to keep them from attacking you.

Once inside the city, you need to try and find the Elder Brain. According to the Seer, you may be able to convince it to withdraw the illithid support of the Valsharess.

You've gained access to the illithid city of Zorvak'Mur. As long as you continue to wear the helm that protects you from the mind flayers' telepathic powers, you should be able to convince the illithid that you are nothing but a slaver visiting their city.

You still need to try and find the Elder Brain. According to the Seer, you may be able to convince it to withdraw the illithid support of the Valsharess.

You've promised to give the Zorvak'Mur Overmind a magical mirror. In exchange, it will convince the Elder Concorde - a collection of illithid Elder Brains - to withdraw their support from the Valsharess.

You've freed a group of slaves from the pens of Zorvak'Mur, and they plan to start a rebellion once you've reached the Elder Brain. Should their revolt succeed, you likely won't have any chance of gaining the support of Zorvak'Mur or the illithid in your cause.

You've betrayed the slave rebellion for the sake of the greater good. By denying Argosus and his followers their freedom, you still have a chance to convince the Zorvak'Mur Elder Brain to help you against the Valsharess.
The illithid of Zorvak'Mur have attacked you. The chances of reaching the Elder Brain now are slim, but if you do it might still be possible to negotiate a treaty with it.

You've destroyed the Elder Brain of Zorvak'Mur, crippling the city. However, your actions have done little to harm the Valsharess, as she will simply draw on the illithid from other areas for her army.
You've unleashed a wave of violence in Zorvak'Mur. Any chance you had of gaining the Elder Brain's support is surely lost.

You've given the magical mirror to the Overmind of Zorvak'Mur. In exchange, it has promised to convince the Elder Concorde - a collection of illithid Overminds - to withdraw their support from the Valsharess.

The only drawback is that you have given the illithid a dangerously powerful artifact. No doubt their entire race will become stronger because of it. Despite your success, you can't help but wonder if the cost was too high.

Knowing how the tale ends, however, is only part of the story. There is evidence in the old tomes that tell of your fate in the years to come, the fate of your companions and the effect your passing had upon the world.

As for the Sleeping Man, there were few who mourned his passing. The Celestials had long since forgotten him and little love was held for him in Baator. On the far-off plane of Limbo, some githzerai still try to live by his teachings. He is remembered best, perhaps, by the bards who still sing your tale. The origin of this cloak dates back to the days when King Richard Garrison held power in the city-state of Gibbonsfeldt. It was crafted for him by his servant, a demented and twisted man named Pony Tall.

Though Pony was not a gifted man, he managed to sew the cloak in just a few days. It was a misshapen thing, barely resembling a cloak at all, but Pony Tall had done the best he could. Wrapping the tattered garment up, he made way to his lord and master.

Enraged by the gift's insult, King Garrison drew his mighty blade and cut Pony down before all the court, his blood staining the ragged cloak a garish red.

Before tossing the garment out with Pony's stricken corpse, the King placed it around his neck to mock its incompetent maker. The courtiers jeered and laughed at its haphazard manufacture.

Upon placing the cloak about his shoulders, however, the King suddenly felt a little stronger, a little wiser, a little younger. Even the night's cold wind no longer chilled to his aging bones.

It has long been said that a fool's blood spilled in a wise king's court holds a magic unlike any other. As a result, the king's wizards have suggested that the cloak's magic came not from any aspect of its fashioning but instead from the corrupted taint of Pony's blood that paints it red.

Whatever the case, the shroud's power is quite remarkable despite the unseemliness of its appearance. To this day in Gibbonsfeldt, lords and ladies don the most hideous garments they can find to celebrate All Fool's Day and the long, wise reign of Richard Garrison.
